{"parentUuid":"6a1b07ad-866e-4b27-b0a8-bd85c7054690","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"dd94e787-6133-4910-b626-76a60ac4c767","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MLxTk9L1LsddwYXLfVMbM9","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Agent Notes — Learned Rules\n2\t\n3\t> Append-mostly. Each rule earned through real experience (post-mortem, drift detection, user correction).\n4\t> Rules here have higher status than convention but lower than constitution.\n5\t\n6\t## Rule Format\n7\t\n8\tUse this template:\n9\t\n10\t```markdown\n11\t### YYYY-MM-DD: [Short rule name]\n12\t**Context**: What situation triggered learning this\n13\t**Rule**: The actionable rule\n14\t**Anti-example**: What was done wrong\n15\t**Correct example**: What should be done instead\n16\t**Severity**: critical | high | medium | low\n17\t**Auto-detect**: yes/no — can a drift signal catch this?\n18\t```\n19\t\n20\t---\n21\t\n22\t## Initial Rules (from charter design)\n23\t\n24\t### 2026-04-23: LLM Never Outputs Numbers\n25\t**Context**: Stock domain risk — LLM-generated numbers in finance lead to real money loss\n26\t**Rule**: LLM never returns numerical values as natural-language output. All numbers come from deterministic Python functions invoked via tool use. LLM only interprets results.\n27\t**Anti-example**:\n28\t```\n29\tLLM output: \"Based on my analysis, the company's ROE is approximately 18%, P/E is around 12, and intrinsic value is roughly 95,000 VND per share.\"\n30\t```\n31\t**Correct example**:\n32\t```\n33\tLLM tool calls:\n34\t  compute_roe(net_income=2_345B, equity=13_120B) → 17.87%\n35\t  compute_pe(price=85_000, eps=7_054) → 12.05\n36\t  compute_intrinsic_value_dcf(...) → 94_523 VND\n37\tLLM output: \"ROE = 17.87% (FY2024), P/E = 12.05 (TTM), DCF intrinsic value = 94,523 VND. Versus current price 85,000 VND, suggests ~11% margin of safety.\"\n38\t```\n39\t**Severity**: critical\n40\t**Auto-detect**: yes — regex for \"approximately\", \"around\", \"roughly\" + numbers in LLM output\n41\t\n42\t### 2026-04-23: Bear Case Required for Every Thesis\n43\t**Context**: Confirmation bias is the #1 retail investor mistake\n44\t**Rule**: Every thesis output must include substantive bear case (≥3 distinct points, each grounded in evidence). System refuses to render thesis without it.\n45\t**Anti-example**: Thesis with bull case + risks section that says \"market volatility, regulatory changes\" (boilerplate)\n46\t**Correct example**: Bear case with specific points like \"Q3 inventory turnover dropped 23% YoY suggesting demand weakness\", \"Major competitor X launched directly competitive product Y in March 2026\", \"Net working capital deterioration of 15% indicates cash flow strain\"\n47\t**Severity**: high\n48\t**Auto-detect**: yes — bear case length + specificity check\n49\t\n50\t### 2026-04-23: Confidence Requires Calibration Data\n51\t**Context**: LLM \"confidence\" is qualitative; user reads numerical values\n52\t**Rule**: Any \"X% confidence\" or \"high/medium/low confidence\" claim must trace to historical hit rate from calibration database. Include `n_samples`, `lookback_period`, `hit_rate` metadata.\n53\t**Anti-example**: \"70% confidence this is a buy\"\n54\t**Correct example**: \"Confidence: MEDIUM (signal pattern: cyclical_bottom_with_dividend; historical n=23 cases since 2018; hit rate 65% over 12 months; lookback=78 months)\"\n55\t**Severity**: high\n56\t**Auto-detect**: partial — flag confidence claims without metadata\n57\t\n58\t### 2026-04-23: Source Provider Disagreement Surfaced\n59\t**Context**: vnstock vs FiinPro vs TCBS sometimes disagree on same data point\n60\t**Rule**: When sources disagree by >1%, output shows divergence explicitly. Never silently pick one.\n61\t**Anti-example**: \"Revenue Q3 2024: 35,000 tỷ\" (silent average or arbitrary pick)\n62\t**Correct example**: \"Revenue Q3 2024: 35,000 tỷ ± 200 tỷ (vnstock: 35,000 / FiinPro: 35,200 / TCBS: 34,800; reconciled with HIGH confidence)\"\n63\t**Severity**: medium\n64\t**Auto-detect**: no (requires source metadata in output template)\n65\t\n66\t---\n67\t\n68\t## Add New Rules Here\n69\t\n70\t### 2026-04-29: Q&A Bundle Skeleton MUST Carry `defer_cycle` Field\n71\t**Context**: While drafting `qa-escalation/references/sample-bundle.md` in S2, I initially omitted `defer_cycle` from the bundle frontmatter — caught on review against Decision 002 § Track 2 R7 mitigation.\n72\t**Rule**: Every Q&A bundle file in `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/` MUST include `defer_cycle: 0` at creation, and increment on every reopening / supersession. SessionStart hook (Track 5) keys can-kicking detection off this field.\n73\t**Anti-example**: Bundle with frontmatter `id / topic / opened_at / expected_answer_by / priority / status` — passes superficial validation but R7 mitigation is invisible.\n74\t**Correct example**: Bundle frontmatter includes `defer_cycle: 0` from creation; every Decision in `related_decisions:` also has `defer_cycles` field syncronized.\n75\t**Severity**: medium\n76\t**Auto-detect**: yes — Track 5 `qa-pending-stale-mover.sh` hook should reject bundles missing the field.\n77\t\n78\t### 2026-04-29: User Communication Idiom — \"ok rồi. continue\" / \"ok continue\" = Trivial Acknowledgment\n79\t**Context**: User in `human-workspace/user_prompt/20260429_03.txt` and via chat replies repeatedly used the idiom \"ok rồi. continue\" or \"ok continue\" as the standard \"I accept the proposed defaults; proceed\" signal in Q&A round acceptance flows.\n80\t**Rule**: Treat both phrases as TRIVIAL acknowledgment in lite-detect (`user-prompt-intake/references/lite-detect-patterns.md`). Do NOT dispatch intent-classifier on these. They specifically mean \"accept all defaults of the most recent agent-proposed bundle / decision\".\n81\t**Anti-example**: Spending 5K context to classify \"ok continue\" via subagent — wasteful and misses the user's stable communication idiom.\n82\t**Correct example**: Lite-detect short-circuits these to `primary_intent: TRIVIAL` + `recommended_action: HANDLE_TRIVIAL`. Continue per `current-execution.md`.\n83\t**Severity**: low (efficiency, not correctness)\n84\t**Auto-detect**: yes — already covered in lite-detect whitelist as \"special idiom\" entry.\n85\t\n86\t### 2026-04-29: Hooks Invoked by Harness Shell Don't Traverse Claude Permission Model\n87\t**Context**: While designing Q&A escalation in S2, I encountered a tension: `Write(human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/**)` is deny-listed for the agent (only humans move files there), but Track 5 hooks may need to write `status: processed` flag inside answered files.\n88\t**Rule**: Hooks invoked by Claude Code harness (configured in `.claude/settings.json` `hooks` section) execute as shell scripts OUTSIDE the agent's tool-permission model. The deny-list applies to the agent's Write/Edit tool calls, not to hook scripts. Therefore hook scripts CAN write to deny-listed paths, but should still respect the spirit (don't pretend to be human-authored content).\n89\t**Anti-example**: Refusing to write a Track 5 hook that updates `status: processed` because \"the agent can't write to answered/\".\n90\t**Correct example**: Hook script writes the `status: processed` flag; agent's tool calls remain blocked. If unsure, prefer sidecar files (`<bundle>.processed`) over in-place edits to keep audit trail crisp.\n91\t**Severity**: medium\n92\t**Auto-detect**: no (design-time consideration)\n93\t\n94\t### 2026-04-29 (post-audit): AP-S2-3 — False Self-Attestation on Measurable Properties\n95\t**Context**: In S2 session log \"verifier-lite pass\" I claimed: \"SKILL.md bodies are 130-160 LOC each…within target\". Adversarial drift audit (background `general-purpose` subagent) measured actual LOC and found `qa-escalation` = 242 (+61% over) and `grill-maximization` = 187 (+25% over). My self-attestation was wrong by ~25-61%, while feeling confident.\n96\t**Rule**: For any property that can be measured deterministically (LOC, byte count, presence-of-field, file-exists), VERIFY with the actual command (`wc -l`, `Glob`, `Grep`) before writing the verifier-lite claim. Do NOT estimate from memory of \"what I just wrote feels about right.\"\n97\t**Anti-example**: \"manual count: SKILL.md bodies are 130-160 LOC each…within target\" written without running `wc -l`.\n98\t**Correct example**: Run `wc -l <file>` for each verified item; quote the actual number. If above ceiling, either trim or document the overrun + grace flag explicitly.\n99\t**Severity**: high (this is the same anti-pattern as orch's CF-DOGFOOD-2 self-attestation — agent claims compliance based on impression, not verification)\n100\t**Auto-detect**: yes — Track 5 hook can grep session logs for `LOC|line count|bodies are.*LOC` claims and require accompanying `wc -l` command in the same session log.\n101\t\n102\t### 2026-04-29 (post-audit): Charter-Tier Items Never Ride Default-Acceptance Bundles\n103\t**Context**: In Round-3 Q&A the agent bundled Q-S1..Q-S5 together. Q-S5 (\"small trusted circle = git-fork single-tenant\") is identity-tier (locks Phase 0-5 architecture, threshold 0.99). The other 4 (Q-S1..Q-S4) were SCOPE-tier (threshold 0.90). User's \"ok continue\" reply absorbed all 5 via the safe-defaults shortcut. This is exactly the orch CF-DOGFOOD-2 pattern UP-02 §1.1 warned about.\n104\t**Rule**: When composing a Q&A bundle, if ANY question is CHARTER-tier (threshold 0.99), split it into a dedicated CHARTER-only bundle. The CHARTER bundle has: explicit-pick options only (no safe agent-defaults), no `D: open answer`-only fields, ALERT notification regardless of priority, and `approval_chain` requires verbatim user phrase quoted in the answered file (not just `ACCEPTED via \"ok continue\"`).\n105\t**Anti-example**: 5 mixed-tier questions in one bundle accepted via \"ok continue\".\n106\t**Correct example**: 4 SCOPE questions in one bundle (defaults OK); 1 CHARTER question in a separate dedicated bundle with explicit confirmation.\n107\t**Severity**: high (charter scope drift is the most damaging drift type)\n108\t**Auto-detect**: yes — drift-detector grep for bundles where ≥1 `level: CHARTER` field appears alongside other levels in the same `related_decisions:` array.\n109\t\n110\t### 2026-04-29 (UP-06): NO Silent File-Defaults — Every Needed Answer via AskUserQuestion Multi-Batch\n111\t**Context**: User in chat after UP-05 turn explicitly corrected: \"tôi sẽ không vào file q&a để trả lời, ví dụ như tôi đang remote-control từ mobile thì sao. cần phải làm cho q&a thực sự hiệu quả chứ không phải làm cho có\". Agent had been writing bundles with N>4 questions, firing 4 via `AskUserQuestion`, then claiming \"rest will default after 24h if user doesn't edit file\". This is exactly the orch CF-DOGFOOD-2 silent-absorption pattern in disguise — for mobile-remote users especially, file-edit is not a real channel.\n112\t**Rule**: Every question agent NEEDS answered MUST be surfaced via `AskUserQuestion`. For >4 questions: multi-batch chain (within-turn `Ask(4) → Ask(4) → ...` or across-turn). Bundle file = pure audit trail; NEVER an input surface with default-after-N-hours fallback. If a question is \"would be nice but not blocking now\" → DO NOT bundle as deferred-default; instead queue in `agent-workspace/memory/observations/queued-grill-<topic>.md` with `fire_when: <track-or-condition>` trigger. Re-grill via Ask when condition activates.\n113\t**Anti-example**: Write 16-question bundle, fire 4 via `Ask`, mark remaining 12 with \"default applies after 24h if user doesn't edit file\". Mobile-remote user never edits file → defaults silently absorb 12 decisions agent never explicitly verified.\n114\t**Correct example**: 16-question bundle → fire 4 via `Ask` → user answers → fire next 4 via `Ask` → ... 4 batches total OR drop questions that aren't truly blocking now (queue them with `fire_when:`). Bundle file logs all 16 with answers from each Ask round; NO \"default\" semantic.\n115\t**Severity**: critical (mobile-remote primary use case; silent absorption is the pattern user explicitly corrected for the third time in this project — UP-02 §1.1, UP-04 G1, UP-06 here).\n116\t**Auto-detect**: yes — drift-detector greps Q&A bundle frontmatter for `pending_in_file:` array OR \"default applies\" string; flag any bundle that has unanswered questions without matching `AskUserQuestion` call OR `queued-grill-*.md` follow-up.\n117\t\n118\t### 2026-04-29 (UP-05): AskUserQuestion 4-Question Limit is Intentional; Multi-Batch is the Workaround\n119\t**Context**: User asked if 4-question limit on `AskUserQuestion` could be bypassed via setting/script/repo. `claude-code-guide` subagent research (2026-04-29) confirmed: limit is intentional design (`maxItems: 4` JSONSchema constraint); NO config flag / env var / hidden setting overrides it.\n120\t**Rule**: For bundles >4 questions, use multi-batch pattern: fire 4 most-critical via `AskUserQuestion` in same turn → record answers → fire next 4 via second `AskUserQuestion` call (or queue file-based for async). Never try to `AskUserQuestion` >4 in one call; tool will reject. The B1=A policy (AskUserQuestion-primary) still holds — multi-batch is the implementation, not a violation.\n121\t**Anti-example**: Try to fire 16-question bundle in one `AskUserQuestion` call (will fail with validation error).\n122\t**Correct example**: 16-question bundle → 4 batches × 4 questions → 4 sequential `AskUserQuestion` calls (or 4 batches across 4 turns) + file audit trail with all 16.\n123\t**Severity**: low (workflow detail, not correctness)\n124\t**Auto-detect**: yes — drift-detector greps for `AskUserQuestion` calls with >4 questions in tool-input (will already fail at runtime; this is belt-and-suspenders).\n125\t\n126\t### 2026-04-29 (UP-05): `--dangerously-skip-permissions` Has Hard-Limit Exceptions (Anthropic-Designed)\n127\t**Context**: User reported autonomous loop breaks when `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag is set but Claude Code still prompts on certain operations. Research via `claude-code-guide` confirmed.\n128\t**Rule**: `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (alias `bypassPermissions` mode) does NOT bypass: (a) writes to `.git/.husky/.vscode/.idea/.claude/` (except `commands/agents/skills` subdirs), (b) writes to `.gitconfig/.bashrc/.zshrc/.mcp.json/.claude.json`, (c) `Skill` tool execution (always prompts), (d) PreToolUse hooks returning `deny` (exit code 2). Hook `{decision: approve}` does NOT override permission system. These are Anthropic-designed limits and CANNOT be bypassed.\n129\t**Anti-example**: Designing autonomous loop that calls `Skill` tool every N steps; loop will pause indefinitely waiting for approval.\n130\t**Correct example**: For autonomous mode, replace `Skill` calls with inline procedures (read SKILL.md content + execute manually) OR gate skill calls to SUPERVISED mode (per UP-05 Q2.1 default policy). Batch any `.git/.claude/` settings changes for end-of-session manual sign-off.\n131\t**Severity**: high (autonomous mode breaker if not respected)\n132\t**Auto-detect**: partial — drift-detector can grep autonomous-mode session for `Skill(` invocations or writes to protected paths; flag.\n133\t\n134\t### 2026-04-29 (UP-04): AskUserQuestion is PRIMARY Q&A Channel (per B1 charter-tier confirmation)\n135\t**Context**: User in `human-workspace/user_prompt/20260429_04.txt` explicitly criticized file-based Q&A (S2 design): \"phải hiển thị ra giao diện q&a do claude code built in cung cấp để human thực sự đọc và verify... hiện tại nhiều q&a và quick answer làm agent bị over và thường có xu hướng chọn default suggest thay vì tự đưa ra decision\". Charter-tier B1 answered \"A: AskUserQuestion ALL bundles, file = audit only\" via AskUserQuestion 2026-04-29T14:05Z.\n136\t**Rule**: The Claude Code built-in `AskUserQuestion` tool is the PRIMARY input surface for ALL Q&A bundles. File-based bundle in `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/<file>.md` becomes audit-trail-only. Every bundle MUST surface its 1-4 most-critical questions via `AskUserQuestion`; bundles >4 questions split into batches. Charter-tier questions ALWAYS via `AskUserQuestion` (never file-only-with-default-acceptance).\n137\t**Anti-example**: Writing a 16-question bundle to `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/` and waiting for human to file-edit. Encourages default-pick shortcut; agent over-defers; sync rate drops.\n138\t**Correct example**: Write 16-question file (audit trail) AND fire `AskUserQuestion` with top-4 critical questions in same turn. Update bundle frontmatter `answered:` array as user picks. Remaining 12 questions follow-up via second `AskUserQuestion` batch or async file-edit if user defers.\n139\t**Severity**: high (encoded in `qa-escalation/SKILL.md § Channel Routing` as BINDING)\n140\t**Auto-detect**: yes — drift-detector greps for `Write(human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/**)` calls without accompanying `AskUserQuestion` tool use in the same session log; flag if missing.\n141\t\n142\t### 2026-04-29 (S3 — Track 5 Loop-Resilience Port): grep -c with || fallback double-counts zero\n143\t**Context**: While testing `scripts/hooks/drift-signals-D1-D8.sh` D3 (charter-mixed bundle detection), bash error fired: `[: 0\\n0: integer expression expected`. Root cause: `VAR=$(grep -cE 'pattern' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)` — when grep finds zero matches, grep -c PRINTS \"0\" AND exits 1, so `|| echo 0` ALSO fires, appending another \"0\". Variable becomes \"0\\n0\", failing integer comparison.\n144\t**Rule**: For `grep -c` capture in bash: do NOT use `|| echo N` fallback (grep already prints 0 on zero matches). Use `|| true` to swallow exit code, then validate with `[[ \"$VAR\" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || VAR=0` for safety. Same pattern applies to `wc -l`, `awk count`, etc. — any tool that prints numeric output AND exits non-zero on no-match.\n145\t**Anti-example**: `COUNT=$(grep -cE 'pattern' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)` — captures \"0\\n0\" on zero matches.\n146\t**Correct example**: `COUNT=$(grep -cE 'pattern' \"$f\" 2>/dev/null || true); [[ \"$COUNT\" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || COUNT=0`.\n147\t**Severity**: low (caught by smoke test; doesn't escape to production)\n148\t**Auto-detect**: yes — Track 9 hook-diagnostics skill can grep hook scripts for `grep -c.*\\|\\| echo` pattern.\n149\t\n150\t### 2026-04-29 (S7 — UP-07 follow-up): Stale-Prompt Reference Check Before Acting\n151\t**Context**: Post-/clear in S7 SessionStart, user submitted \"continue UP-07 work — check if claude-code-guide research returned + synthesize options + fire AskUserQuestion\" referencing work CLOSED in S6 via D-004. Agent had no deterministic detection; was forced to fire clarifying AskUserQuestion, blocking autonomous flow. Full RCA in `agent-workspace/memory/mistake-log.md § M-S7-1`.\n152\t**Rule**: When user prompt references `UP-[0-9]+`, `D-[0-9]+`, `Track [0-9]+(\\.[0-9a-z]+)?`, or `S[0-9]+`, the `stale-prompt-detector.sh` UserPromptSubmit hook cross-checks `up-intake-log.md` + `decisions/*.md` + `current-execution.md`. If hook emits \"STALE-PROMPT DETECTOR\" warning in additionalContext: agent MUST first surface closure status (1-2 sentences citing linked decision/session) before any action. Only re-do work if user explicitly picks \"redo\" via AskUserQuestion or unambiguous text. Per UP-06 NO-Silent-Default + this RCA.\n153\t**Anti-example**: Receive \"continue UP-07 work\" post-/clear → silently dispatch claude-code-guide subagent again + duplicate the AskUserQuestion sequence + re-ship D-004 (waste 30-50K tokens; risk superseding ACCEPTED decision without rationale).\n154\t**Correct example**: Receive same prompt → hook injects warning \"UP-07 CLOSED via D-004\" → agent surfaces \"UP-07 đã closed at S6 via D-004 (180K/220K/250K threshold band ACCEPTED). Bạn muốn (a) confirm + move to S7, (b) revisit with new research, (c) other?\" via AskUserQuestion → proceed per pick.\n155\t**Severity**: high (in autonomous mode this would block infinite loop, since no human to clarify; deterministic hook detection is the only viable Guardian per AP-23).\n156\t**Auto-detect**: yes — `scripts/hooks/stale-prompt-detector.sh` is the auto-detector itself. Drift signal: ANY UserPromptSubmit to a prompt matching the regex without invoking this hook = drift.\n157\t\n158\t### 2026-04-29 (S7 — UP-07 follow-up): Continue-Injector Gated by autonomous_mode [SUPERSEDED by S8 entry below]\n159\t**Context**: `scripts/hooks/continue-injector.ps1` SendKeys \"continue\" + Enter to fresh TUI on every SessionStart (verified 3 log files same day). Designed for autonomous mode (no human → injector starts loop). But ungated firing in SUPERVISED mode caused race conditions with user typing + re-triggered work-already-done flows.\n160\t**Rule**: `session-start-bootstrap.sh` MUST grep `autonomous_mode` field from `agent-workspace/memory/current-execution.md` BEFORE spawning continue-injector. Spawn ONLY if `autonomous_mode=true`. In SUPERVISED mode (default until Track 7), log \"SKIPPED continue-injector\" and exit.\n161\t**Anti-example**: Hook unconditionally spawns injector → user types \"continue UP-07 work...\" simultaneously with injector typing \"continue\" → race condition: which prompt reaches LLM first? Both submitted? Confused state.\n162\t**Correct example**: Hook reads autonomous_mode → false (current) → skip spawn. User types prompt at their pace. Logged: `SessionStart-bootstrap SKIPPED continue-injector (autonomous_mode=false)`.\n163\t**Severity**: medium (race condition rarely produces wrong outcome but creates user confusion + adds non-deterministic noise).\n164\t**Auto-detect**: yes — drift-detector greps session-start-bootstrap.sh for unconditional `Start-Process.*continue-injector` without preceding `autonomous_mode` check.\n165\t**Superseded-by**: 2026-04-29 (S8 mid-session) entry below — source-specific gating chosen over blanket gate.\n166\t\n167\t### 2026-04-29 (S8 mid-session — user complaint \"no continue, why? fix\"): Source-Specific Continue-Injector Gating\n168\t**Context**: S7 blanket gate (autonomous_mode=true required) made `/clear` UX broken — user `/clear`-ed at 17:51:55, expected checkpoint resume; injector skipped at 17:51:57; user manually typed at 18:18:59 (27-min wait). Race-condition concern from S7 was about `startup` (claude first-run, user likely typing) — does NOT apply to `/clear` (explicit user action with predictable ~5s window) or `resume` (user just invoked `claude --resume`, expects continuation).\n169\t**Rule**: `session-start-bootstrap.sh` source-specific gating:\n170\t- `source=clear` → fire continue-injector UNCONDITIONALLY (low race risk; user just cleared and expects auto-resume from checkpoints/latest.md)\n171\t- `source=resume` → fire continue-injector UNCONDITIONALLY (user invoked claude --resume; expects continuation)\n172\t- `source=startup` → fire ONLY if `autonomous_mode=true` (preserve S7 race-fix; user opening fresh claude likely has prompt in mind)\n173\t**Why safe in SUPERVISED**: stale-prompt-detector.sh line 26 short-circuits on bare \"continue\" prompt (regex `^[[:space:]]*(continue|ok|yes|y|n|no|done)[[:space:]]*$`) → no spurious stale-warning. Agent reads SessionStart additionalContext + checkpoint to determine next action; \"continue\" is just the wake-up trigger.\n174\t**Anti-example**: Hook gates ALL sources behind autonomous_mode → user `/clear`-s mid-session expecting checkpoint resume → silent 27-min hang waiting for user to manually re-prompt → autonomous flow effectively broken in supervised mode.\n175\t**Correct example**: Hook reads source=clear → spawn injector unconditionally → fresh TUI receives \"continue\" 2.5s after /clear → agent reads checkpoint + queued-grill-master + current-execution.md → resumes at next_action. Logged: `SessionStart-bootstrap spawned continue-injector (source=clear (explicit user action))`.\n176\t**Severity**: high (UX-blocking; user explicitly complained — broken auto-resume = broken supervised-mode autonomy).\n177\t**Auto-detect**: yes — drift-detector greps session-start-bootstrap.sh for the `case \"$SOURCE\" in clear) ... ;;` block; absence = drift back to S7 blanket gate.\n178\t\n179\t### 2026-04-29 (post-audit): Pre-Amendment Delta Summary Mandatory for Large REV-N\n180\t**Context**: REV-2 added 30+ amendments + budget delta 940K→1.3M tokens (+38%) — user \"ok continue\" approved both. The agent never explicitly surfaced \"you are ratifying 30+ amendments and +38% budget\" in headline form. UP-02 §1.3 warned: \"human đối mặt hàng chục spec/document quá tải nếu không sắp xếp khoa học\".\n181\t**Rule**: For any REV-N that adds ≥10 amendments OR increases budget by ≥25% OR adds tracks OR changes sequencing — author a \"Delta Summary\" block at the top of the Q&A bundle headline AND in the notification body. Make the magnitude visible before requesting approval.\n182\t**Anti-example**: REV-2 amendments tucked inside D-002 § Amendments, with budget increase noted on line 466.\n183\t**Correct example**: Q&A bundle headline starts with `## REV-N Delta Summary` block listing amendments_added / budget_delta / sequencing_delta / track_delta / what_user_commits_to / what_user_can_revert.\n184\t**Severity**: medium\n185\t**Auto-detect**: partial — drift-detector compares D-NNN status fields (REV-N) against presence of `Delta Summary` block in any related Q&A bundle.\n186\t\n187\t### 2026-04-29 (S10 — Track 5.5d.1): Bash Hook ERR-Trap Silent Failure (set -uo pipefail + trap ERR + `[ x ] && Y`)\n188\t**Context**: `scripts/hooks/component-telemetry.sh` had been silently bricked since S8 ship. JSONL telemetry stream did not exist on disk despite hook being wired in `.claude/settings.json` for SessionStart/PostToolUse/SubagentStop. Discovered in S10 D-2 smoke test when the new `learning-data/events/*.ndjson` also didn't write. Root cause traced via `bash -x`: 3 patterns trip the `trap 'exit 0' ERR` trap when LHS is FALSE — `[ \"$TOKENS_REAL\" -lt 0 ] && TOKENS_REAL=0` (line 111), `([ x ] || [ y ]) && Z=0` (line 124), `[ \"$PAYLOAD_DECISION\" = \"deny\" ] && FAILURE_MODE='\"H\"'` (line 226). Plus `local session=\"$1\" ts_file=\"...${session}\"` (line 115) trips `set -u` because `session` is unbound at parse-time of `ts_file` in the same `local` declaration. Git Bash on Windows appears to fire ERR on `[ x ] && Y` even though Bash manual exempts conditional context — empirical not theoretical guidance.\n189\t**Rule**: Bash hook scripts running with `set -uo pipefail` + `trap 'exit 0' ERR` (or any non-noop ERR trap) MUST: (a) use `if [ x ]; then Y; fi` instead of `[ x ] && Y` when LHS may be FALSE; (b) split `local A=$1 B=$A` into separate `local` declarations to avoid same-line cross-references under `set -u`; (c) verify smoke-test produces ACTUAL file writes — not just \"exit 0\" return code, which the trap can fake.\n190\t**Anti-example**: `[ \"$VAR\" -lt 0 ] && VAR=0` (LHS often FALSE → ERR fires → silent exit 0 → script appears to succeed but does nothing). Same: `local a=\"$1\" b=\"${MEMORY_DIR}/.x-${a}\"` (b uses a before a is set; `set -u` fires).\n191\t**Correct example**: `if [ \"$VAR\" -lt 0 ]; then VAR=0; fi` and `local a=\"$1\"; local b=\"${MEMORY_DIR}/.x-${a}\"` (separate declarations).\n192\t**Severity**: HIGH (bricked telemetry stream for ~3-4 sessions undetected; \"shipped S8\" claim was vacuous).\n193\t**Auto-detect**: candidate for new drift signal D10 or extension to existing `loc-ceiling-check.sh`. Proposed scan: any `scripts/hooks/*.sh` with `trap '.*' ERR` + `set -.*u.*` AND containing pattern `\\[ .* \\] &&` (single-line conditional) OR `local \\w+=.*\\$\\{?\\w+\\}?.*\\w+=.*\\$\\1` (same-line cross-ref). Promote to deterministic check at S15 Track 7 if S11/S12 surfaces more occurrences.\n194\t\n195\t### 2026-04-29 (S10 — Track 5.5d.1): Glob + Read + Bash File-Ops All Honor Boundary Deny — Triple-Enforcement\n196\t**Context**: After adding `Read(agent-workspace/learning-data/events/**)` to `.claude/settings.json` deny + gitignore'ing the same paths, agent attempted to verify file content via 3 paths and found ALL denied: (1) `Read` tool → \"File is in a directory that is denied by your permission settings\"; (2) `Bash(cat:*)` and `Bash(wc:*)` though in allow list → harness denies because path-deny rule intersects; (3) `Glob agent-workspace/learning-data/events/*` → \"No files found\" because Glob honors .gitignore. The boundary CANNOT be circumvented from main session without explicit permission removal.\n197\t**Rule**: For runtime-deny boundaries on write-heavy data stores: combine (1) `.gitignore` exclusion (free, makes Glob blind) + (2) `.claude/settings.json` Read/Write/Edit deny rules on path globs (cheap, blocks tool families) + (3) drift signal scanning code paths for boundary-leaking references (e.g., D9 in drift-signals-D1-D9.sh). Any one alone is partial; all three is hardest enforcement available short of OS-level isolation.\n198\t**Anti-example**: Add only deny rule without gitignore — agent can still Glob the file paths and see they exist (information leak about what's being collected). Add only gitignore without deny — agent can still Read directly via known path.\n199\t**Correct example**: D-005 § 5.5d.1 architecture: events/+archive/ have all three. index/+dogfood/+loop/ have none (read-allowed; tracked).\n200\t**Severity**: low (validation of design intent; not a bug fix — informational).\n201\t**Auto-detect**: yes — drift-detector can grep for paths under `agent-workspace/` that are write-only-by-design (e.g., events/) appearing in skill/agent/command files (D9-equivalent). Also: when adding new boundary, lint that all 3 layers are configured.\n202\t\n203\t### 2026-04-29 (S10 — Track 5.5d.1): Append-Only Contract Allows Stale Filename References in History\n204\t**Context**: When renaming `drift-signals-D1-D8.sh` → `drift-signals-D1-D9.sh` per D-005 § 5.5d.1, found 26 callers across the project. 4 are LIVE (`.claude/settings.json` + `.claude/manifest.yaml` 3× + 2 attach skill files); 22 are in append-only history (`agent-workspace/memory/{sessions,checkpoints,decisions,observations,drift-logs}/` + `agent-workspace/raw-sessions/` + `human-workspace/{q-and-a,notifications}/`). Updating the 22 historical references would rewrite history and violate workspace dualism (D-002). Leaving them stale was the chosen approach.\n205\t**Rule**: When renaming script/file/symbol referenced from BOTH live config AND historical append-only artifacts: update LIVE callers only (settings.json, manifest, skills, agents, commands, scripts); leave historical references stale. Past sessions/checkpoints/decisions/notifications are time-frozen snapshots — accuracy is \"what was true at session-N\", not \"what is true now\". A grep audit (`Grep oldname .claude/ scripts/` returning 0) is the LIVE-clean signal.\n206\t**Anti-example**: Run `find . -name '*.md' | xargs sed -i 's/old-name/new-name/g'` — rewrites 22 historical files; obscures the rename event in git diff; future audits reading old session logs see modern filename and lose temporal context.\n207\t**Correct example**: Update only `.claude/`, `scripts/`, and other LIVE config; document the choice in session log + add 1-line cross-reference in renamed file's header (e.g., \"renamed from D1-D8 in S10 per D-005 § 5.5d.1\").\n208\t**Severity**: low (process discipline; not a bug).\n209\t**Auto-detect**: partial — drift-detector can grep `Grep oldname .claude/ scripts/` after rename commits; non-zero match = drift. Historical references in memory/, raw-sessions/, q-and-a/ are EXEMPT from this check.\n210\t\n211\t### 2026-04-29 (S11 — Track 5.5d.2): Phase 0 Hook Portability — Bash + Node + POSIX Only\n212\t**Context**: Track 5.5d.2 index-rebuild hook needed RAG-style indexer. D-005 listed SQLite FTS5 as preferred Phase 0 choice in deliverables prose. Pre-flight `command -v sqlite3` returned not-found on Windows Git Bash (current dev environment for project owner). Continuing with sqlite3 would have produced a hook that silently no-ops on dev machine — same failure shape as L-S10-1 silent ERR-trap. Picked \"simple bash + node-eval\" branch from D-005 § Open Questions instead. Manifest = JSON via printf+node; sample dump = NDJSON copy via cat+tail; state marker = JSON via printf+node-eval read.\n213\t**Rule**: Phase 0 hooks running on bare dev machines MUST limit dependencies to: `bash` + `node` (project already requires for telemetry) + standard POSIX (`find`, `grep`, `wc`, `mv`, `rm`, `cat`, `stat`, `sort`, `tail`, `head`, `tr`, `sed`, `awk`, `mkdir`, `printf`, `date`). NOT permitted: `sqlite3`, `duckdb`, `jq`, `python3` (project uses but not at hook level), `curl`/`wget` (no network from hooks), language runtimes beyond node. When richer indexing/processing is needed, defer to Phase 1+ where deployment ships dependencies in a Docker image with verified `requirements.txt` / `package.json`.\n214\t**Anti-example**: `sqlite3 db.fts < index.sql` in hook script — works on Linux dev machines, silently fails on Win Git Bash → boundary-hook bricked invisibly.\n215\t**Correct example**: `find events/ -name '*.ndjson' | sort | xargs cat | tail -100 > index/recent-sample.ndjson` — bash + POSIX only; works everywhere bash runs.\n216\t**Severity**: medium (portability gates the bootstrap promise of \"hook works on any dev machine\").\n217\t**Auto-detect**: yes — extension to `loc-ceiling-check.sh` or new `bash-hook-lint.sh`: scan `scripts/hooks/*.sh` for non-whitelisted command invocations (sqlite3, duckdb, python3, jq, curl, wget); flag with severity HIGH if found in Phase 0 hook. Promote to constitutional rule at Track 7 (S15) — candidate `agent-workspace/constitution/financial-data-protocol.md` § Phase 0 portability.\n218\t\n219\t### 2026-04-29 (S11 — Track 5.5d.2): Spec Internal Inconsistency Surfaces at IMPL Time → IMPL-Tier Resolves\n220\t**Context**: D-005 § 5.5d.1 deliverables prose: `agent-workspace/learning-data/{events,index,archive}/`. D-005 § 5.5d.2 deliverables prose: `agent-workspace/memory/learning-data/index/categories-<TS>.md` (note: `memory/` prefix). These two paths are inconsistent. S10 implementation chose §5.5d.1 layout; permissions in `.claude/settings.json` (`allow Write(agent-workspace/learning-data/{index,dogfood,loop}/**)`), README boundary contract, and `.gitkeep` files are all aligned with §5.5d.1. S11 IMPL faced choice: follow §5.5d.2 prose (split tree under memory/) or §5.5d.1 layout (single tree). Chose §5.5d.1 — alignment with downstream artifacts wins; §5.5d.2 prose treated as drafting bug. Documented as IMPL-S11-2 in session log + carry-over for D-005 amendment at S15 Track 7.\n221\t**Rule**: When IMPL agent finds spec internal inconsistency at execution time: (a) resolve in favor of the layout/wording that downstream artifacts (permissions, README, gitkeep, tests, existing implementations) are already aligned with — alignment cost is real, prose changes are cheap; (b) document the resolution as IMPL-tier decision in session log with explicit \"IMPL-S<N>-<M>\" identifier; (c) surface the inconsistency for spec amendment at next planning boundary via append-only carry-over note in checkpoint + current-execution.md; (d) DO NOT block ship to wait for ratification — the inconsistency is in source-of-record, not in implementation; agent's call is the right call until amended.\n222\t**Anti-example**: Halt S11 ship to ask user \"which path layout?\" when 5/6 downstream artifacts are already aligned with one — this re-raises a settled question and inflates cycle time. Or: silently follow the latest-written prose without surfacing the inconsistency — future readers can't audit which layout is canonical.\n223\t**Correct example**: IMPL-S11-2 in session-11.md + checkpoint/latest.md \"Open carry-over for S15 Track 7\" + current-execution.md S11 carry-over block — three linked notes ensure D-005 amendment is unmistakable next planning cycle.\n224\t**Severity**: medium (recurring spec-drafting risk; Spec-as-source butterfly = drift signal D4 territory).\n225\t**Auto-detect**: partial — drift-detector D4 already scans for spec ↔ code dangling refs. Extension: when same decision file references two paths for the \"same artifact concept\" within different sections, flag as INTERNAL-INCONSISTENCY. Promote to formal rule in `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md` § \"When spec inconsistency surfaces at IMPL time\" at Track 7 (S15).\n226\t\n227\t### 2026-04-29 (S12 / Track 5.5d.3 dogfood): Self-Learning / Outer-Loop Claims Require Deterministic Metric Function\n228\t**Context**: S12 dogfooded `stanfordnlp/dspy@db83e5ad` (research-scanner dispatch result, agent-pick-1 from D-005 § 5.5d.3). Pattern insight from DSPy: every self-improving pipeline's optimizer requires a `metric` function returning a score from deterministic code — the LLM does not score itself. Mapping that onto stockforge's harness surfaced a gap: S11's L-1 classification produced bucket distributions (`0/0/0/49/11`) but emitted **no metric** comparing run N+1 to run N. Without a metric, no version of the loop can be substantiated as \"improved\" over baseline. The Karpathy outer-loop framing artifact (S12 D5) cannot answer \"was the experiment better than the prior baseline?\" without one.\n229\t**Rule**: Any \"self-learning\", \"Karpathy outer-loop\", or \"harness-improvement\" claim authored in stockforge (now or future) MUST cite a deterministic metric function (Python or bash, no LLM judgment) with: (a) explicit formula, (b) baseline value with `n_samples` + `as_of`, (c) target threshold, (d) falsification condition. If no metric exists → describe the experiment (\"we tried X\"), do NOT claim improvement (\"X improved Y\"). Per charter P8 calibration-over-confidence + P9 no-LLM-math.\n230\t**Anti-example**: A Karpathy framing artifact that says \"we deepened classification quality by adding fail-mode wire-in\" without a metric to prove the deepening — the claim collapses to vibes; future agent reading it cannot replicate the verdict.\n231\t**Correct example**: `agent-workspace/learning-data/loop/20260429T131608Z-experiment-frame.md` § Measurement plan — declares `failure_mode_populated_rate = count(events.failure_mode!=null) / count(events)`; baseline 0.0% (n=60, S11); target ≥8.3%; falsification = \"rate stays 0% AND log shows failures occurred\". Deterministic, falsifiable, calibrated.\n232\t**Severity**: high (without this, every self-learning iteration becomes a vibes-based feedback loop — exact failure mode charter principle 8 was written to prevent).\n233\t**Auto-detect**: yes — Track 5.5d.2 `learning-index-rebuild.sh` can be extended (S13) to scan `learning-data/loop/*-experiment-frame.md` for missing `metric_function:` frontmatter field; soft-warn at Stop hook. Promotion target priority hook>skill>charter (cheapest first) per D-005 § 5.5d.3 promotion path.\n234\t\n235\t### 2026-04-29 (S13-pre drift audit): `head -1` of Unscoped Grep Returns Wrong Element on Chained Lists\n236\t**Context**: `scripts/hooks/session-export-raw.sh` SessionEnd hook ran 11 times across S1-S12 but produced only 2 raw-session files (`session-1.md` + `session-5.md`). Other 10 sessions overwrote into one of the two. Drift audit S13-pre traced to line 33: `SESSION_N=\"$(grep -oE 'S[0-9]+' \"$EXEC_FILE\" | head -1 | sed 's/^S//')\"`. The `**Session N**:` line in current-execution.md lists the FULL chain `S1 → S2 → ... → S<latest>`, so `head -1` always returned S1 — the FIRST element, not the active session. Result: 10/12 raw transcripts lost provenance (UP-05 directive about source-of-truth context violated for ~83% of sessions).\n237\t**Rule**: When extracting \"current/active/latest\" from a list-bearing data file: NEVER use `head -1` on unscoped grep over the entire file. Either (a) scope grep to a specific line/section, OR (b) use `sort -n | tail -1` to find the largest, OR (c) use an explicit marker like `S<N> NEXT`. The smoke test for \"is this extracting the right element\" is to run it against a chain like `S1 → S2 → S13 NEXT` and verify it returns S13 (or whatever current session indicator dictates).\n238\t**Anti-example**: `grep -oE 'S[0-9]+' \"$EXEC_FILE\" | head -1` when file contains chain \"S1 → S2 → ... → S13 NEXT\".\n239\t**Correct example**: `grep -oE 'S[0-9]+[[:space:]]+NEXT' \"$EXEC_FILE\" | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+'` (uses explicit NEXT marker) OR `grep -E '^\\*\\*Session N\\*\\*:' \"$EXEC_FILE\" | grep -oE 'S[0-9]+' | sed 's/^S//' | sort -n | tail -1` (scoped grep + numerical sort). Both return 13 for the chain above.\n240\t**Severity**: high (provenance loss; UP-05 directive violation; pattern can recur in any \"latest item\" extraction in hooks).\n241\t**Auto-detect**: yes — bash-hook-lint can scan `scripts/hooks/*.sh` for pattern `grep -oE '[A-Z][0-9]+' .* | head -1` (or similar list-extracting greps with head -1) → flag for review. Promote to constitution at S15 Track 7 paired with L-S11-1 Phase 0 portability rule.\n242\t\n243\t### 2026-04-29 (S13 / Track 5.5c.3 wire-in): Producer-Consumer Log Path Mismatch Silently Nulled Telemetry Field\n244\t**Context**: `scripts/hooks/component-telemetry.sh` `correlate_failure_mode()` was reading `$MEMORY_DIR/.autonomous-stop-watchdog.log` since S8 ship. NO hook ever wrote that path. Real signals lived at `.session-hooks.log` (CLIFF + drift entries) and `.autonomous-premature-windown-alert.log` (mode-C alerts). Result: all 60 events at S11 L-1 had `failure_mode: null`. Misclassified as \"harness too clean to instrument\" in S11 caveat #2; actually was producer-consumer disconnect. Discovered S13 by tracing watchdog writers (`grep -r '.autonomous-stop-watchdog.log' scripts/` → 0 producers; `grep -r '.session-hooks.log' scripts/` → multiple producers).\n245\t**Rule**: When a hook claims to \"correlate\" between two logs (one writing, one reading), smoke-test the producer-consumer path: (a) `grep -r '<log-path>'` returns ≥1 producer AND ≥1 consumer; (b) feed a synthetic event through the consumer and verify the field populates. If either gate fails → wire-in is vacuous; the field will silently stay at default forever. Each rule earned through real experience (post-mortem, drift detection, user correction).\n> Rules here have higher status than convention but lower than constitution.\n\n## Rule Format\n\nUse this template:\n\n```markdown\n### YYYY-MM-DD: [Short rule name]\n**Context**: What situation triggered learning this\n**Rule**: The actionable rule\n**Anti-example**: What was done wrong\n**Correct example**: What should be done instead\n**Severity**: critical | high | medium | low\n**Auto-detect**: yes/no — can a drift signal catch this?\n```\n\n---\n\n## Initial Rules (from charter design)\n\n### 2026-04-23: LLM Never Outputs Numbers\n**Context**: Stock domain risk — LLM-generated numbers in finance lead to real money loss\n**Rule**: LLM never returns numerical values as natural-language output. All numbers come from deterministic Python functions invoked via tool use. LLM only interprets results.\n**Anti-example**:\n```\nLLM output: \"Based on my analysis, the company's ROE is approximately 18%, P/E is around 12, and intrinsic value is roughly 95,000 VND per share.\"\n```\n**Correct example**:\n```\nLLM tool calls:\n  compute_roe(net_income=2_345B, equity=13_120B) → 17.87%\n  compute_pe(price=85_000, eps=7_054) → 12.05\n  compute_intrinsic_value_dcf(...) → 94_523 VND\nLLM output: \"ROE = 17.87% (FY2024), P/E = 12.05 (TTM), DCF intrinsic value = 94,523 VND. Versus current price 85,000 VND, suggests ~11% margin of safety.\"\n```\n**Severity**: critical\n**Auto-detect**: yes — regex for \"approximately\", \"around\", \"roughly\" + numbers in LLM output\n\n### 2026-04-23: Bear Case Required for Every Thesis\n**Context**: Confirmation bias is the #1 retail investor mistake\n**Rule**: Every thesis output must include substantive bear case (≥3 distinct points, each grounded in evidence). System refuses to render thesis without it.\n**Anti-example**: Thesis with bull case + risks section that says \"market volatility, regulatory changes\" (boilerplate)\n**Correct example**: Bear case with specific points like \"Q3 inventory turnover dropped 23% YoY suggesting demand weakness\", \"Major competitor X launched directly competitive product Y in March 2026\", \"Net working capital deterioration of 15% indicates cash flow strain\"\n**Severity**: high\n**Auto-detect**: yes — bear case length + specificity check\n\n### 2026-04-23: Confidence Requires Calibration Data\n**Context**: LLM \"confidence\" is qualitative; user reads numerical values\n**Rule**: Any \"X% confidence\" or \"high/medium/low confidence\" claim must trace to historical hit rate from calibration database. Include `n_samples`, `lookback_period`, `hit_rate` metadata.\n**Anti-example**: \"70% confidence this is a buy\"\n**Correct example**: \"Confidence: MEDIUM (signal pattern: cyclical_bottom_with_dividend; historical n=23 cases since 2018; hit rate 65% over 12 months; lookback=78 months)\"\n**Severity**: high\n**Auto-detect**: partial — flag confidence claims without metadata\n\n### 2026-04-23: Source Provider Disagreement Surfaced\n**Context**: vnstock vs FiinPro vs TCBS sometimes disagree on same data point\n**Rule**: When sources disagree by >1%, output shows divergence explicitly. Never silently pick one.\n**Anti-example**: \"Revenue Q3 2024: 35,000 tỷ\" (silent average or arbitrary pick)\n**Correct example**: \"Revenue Q3 2024: 35,000 tỷ ± 200 tỷ (vnstock: 35,000 / FiinPro: 35,200 / TCBS: 34,800; reconciled with HIGH confidence)\"\n**Severity**: medium\n**Auto-detect**: no (requires source metadata in output template)\n\n---\n\n## Add New Rules Here\n\n### 2026-04-29: Q&A Bundle Skeleton MUST Carry `defer_cycle` Field\n**Context**: While drafting `qa-escalation/references/sample-bundle.md` in S2, I initially omitted `defer_cycle` from the bundle frontmatter — caught on review against Decision 002 § Track 2 R7 mitigation.\n**Rule**: Every Q&A bundle file in `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/` MUST include `defer_cycle: 0` at creation, and increment on every reopening / supersession. JSONL telemetry stream did not exist on disk despite hook being wired in `.claude/settings.json` for SessionStart/PostToolUse/SubagentStop. Discovered in S10 D-2 smoke test when the new `learning-data/events/*.ndjson` also didn't write. Root cause traced via `bash -x`: 3 patterns trip the `trap 'exit 0' ERR` trap when LHS is FALSE — `[ \"$TOKENS_REAL\" -lt 0 ] && TOKENS_REAL=0` (line 111), `([ x ] || [ y ]) && Z=0` (line 124), `[ \"$PAYLOAD_DECISION\" = \"deny\" ] && FAILURE_MODE='\"H\"'` (line 226). Plus `local session=\"$1\" ts_file=\"...${session}\"` (line 115) trips `set -u` because `session` is unbound at parse-time of `ts_file` in the same `local` declaration. Git Bash on Windows appears to fire ERR on `[ x ] && Y` even though Bash manual exempts conditional context — empirical not theoretical guidance.\n**Rule**: Bash hook scripts running with `set -uo pipefail` + `trap 'exit 0' ERR` (or any non-noop ERR trap) MUST: (a) use `if [ x ]; then Y; fi` instead of `[ x ] && Y` when LHS may be FALSE; (b) split `local A=$1 B=$A` into separate `local` declarations to avoid same-line cross-references under `set -u`; (c) verify smoke-test produces ACTUAL file writes — not just \"exit 0\" return code, which the trap can fake.\n**Anti-example**: `[ \"$VAR\" -lt 0 ] && VAR=0` (LHS often FALSE → ERR fires → silent exit 0 → script appears to succeed but does nothing). Same: `local a=\"$1\" b=\"${MEMORY_DIR}/.x-${a}\"` (b uses a before a is set; `set -u` fires).\n**Correct example**: `if [ \"$VAR\" -lt 0 ]; then VAR=0; fi` and `local a=\"$1\"; local b=\"${MEMORY_DIR}/.x-${a}\"` (separate declarations).\n**Severity**: HIGH (bricked telemetry stream for ~3-4 sessions undetected; \"shipped S8\" claim was vacuous).\n**Auto-detect**: candidate for new drift signal D10 or extension to existing `loc-ceiling-check.sh`. Promote to deterministic check at S15 Track 7 if S11/S12 surfaces more occurrences.\n\n### 2026-04-29 (S10 — Track 5.5d.1): Glob + Read + Bash File-Ops All Honor Boundary Deny — Triple-Enforcement\n**Context**: After adding `Read(agent-workspace/learning-data/events/**)` to `.claude/settings.json` deny + gitignore'ing the same paths, agent attempted to verify file content via 3 paths and found ALL denied: (1) `Read` tool → \"File is in a directory that is denied by your permission settings\"; (2) `Bash(cat:*)` and `Bash(wc:*)` though in allow list → harness denies because path-deny rule intersects; (3) `Glob agent-workspace/learning-data/events/*` → \"No files found\" because Glob honors .gitignore. {"parentUuid":"6cb4ecfc-4dd3-4c9d-9976-94c4687ffbe6","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"dd94e787-6133-4910-b626-76a60ac4c767","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KB7nPSRbkhRLnDxaiYC9gx","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t---\n2\tname: postgres-pgvector\n3\tdescription: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n4\t---\n5\t\n6\t# Skill: Postgres + pgvector + TimescaleDB\n7\t\n8\t## Purpose\n9\t\n10\tConsistent schema patterns leveraging Postgres 16 extensions for Vietnamese stock market data.\n11\t\n12\t## Extensions Used\n13\t\n14\t```sql\n15\tCREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS \"uuid-ossp\";    -- UUID generation\n16\tCREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS \"pg_trgm\";      -- Fuzzy text search (Vietnamese)\n17\tCREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS \"vector\";       -- pgvector for embeddings\n18\tCREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS \"timescaledb\";  -- Time-series (prices, sentiment)\n19\t```\n20\t\n21\t## Table Design Patterns\n22\t\n23\t### Aggregate Root Table\n24\t\n25\t```sql\n26\tCREATE TABLE theses (\n27\t  -- Identity\n28\t  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),\n29\t  \n30\t  -- References\n31\t  ticker TEXT NOT NULL,\n32\t  user_id UUID NOT NULL,\n33\t  \n34\t  -- State\n35\t  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'active', 'closed')),\n36\t  \n37\t  -- Business content (JSONB for flexible structure)\n38\t  bull_case JSONB NOT NULL,\n39\t  bear_case JSONB NOT NULL,\n40\t  catalysts JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',\n41\t  \n42\t  -- Calibration\n43\t  confidence_score NUMERIC(4,3) CHECK (confidence_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),\n44\t  hit_rate_basis INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- N past theses of this type\n45\t  \n46\t  -- Temporal\n47\t  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n48\t  submitted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,\n49\t  closed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,\n50\t  \n51\t  -- Audit\n52\t  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n53\t  version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1  -- optimistic locking\n54\t);\n55\t\n56\tCREATE INDEX idx_theses_ticker ON theses(ticker, created_at DESC);\n57\tCREATE INDEX idx_theses_status ON theses(status) WHERE status IN ('draft', 'active');\n58\t```\n59\t\n60\t### Point-in-Time Integrity (Fundamentals)\n61\t\n62\tEvery fundamental data row MUST have both dates:\n63\t\n64\t```sql\n65\tCREATE TABLE financial_statements (\n66\t  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),\n67\t  ticker TEXT NOT NULL,\n68\t  \n69\t  -- CRITICAL: point-in-time integrity (I-S2)\n70\t  period_end DATE NOT NULL,      -- what period this covers\n71\t  filing_date DATE NOT NULL,     -- when it became public knowledge\n72\t  \n73\t  -- Financials (all in VND million)\n74\t  revenue BIGINT,\n75\t  net_income BIGINT,\n76\t  total_assets BIGINT,\n77\t  total_equity BIGINT,\n78\t  \n79\t  -- Source\n80\t  source TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('vnstock', 'fiinpro', 'manual')),\n81\t  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n82\t  \n83\t  UNIQUE(ticker, period_end, filing_date, source)\n84\t);\n85\t\n86\tCREATE INDEX idx_financial_ticker_period ON financial_statements(ticker, filing_date DESC, period_end DESC);\n87\t```\n88\t\n89\tBacktest query MUST use filing_date filter:\n90\t```sql\n91\t-- CORRECT: filters by when data was known (avoids look-ahead bias)\n92\tSELECT * FROM financial_statements\n93\tWHERE ticker = 'VCB'\n94\t  AND filing_date <= '2024-03-31'::date\n95\tORDER BY period_end DESC\n96\tLIMIT 1;\n97\t\n98\t-- WRONG: would introduce look-ahead bias in backtest\n99\t-- SELECT * FROM financial_statements WHERE ticker = 'VCB' ORDER BY period_end DESC LIMIT 1;\n100\t```\n101\t\n102\t### Event Log Table\n103\t\n104\t```sql\n105\tCREATE TABLE domain_events (\n106\t  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),\n107\t  aggregate_id UUID NOT NULL,\n108\t  aggregate_type TEXT NOT NULL,\n109\t  event_type TEXT NOT NULL,\n110\t  event_version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n111\t  payload JSONB NOT NULL,\n112\t  occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n113\t  published_at TIMESTAMPTZ,\n114\t  sequence_num BIGSERIAL NOT NULL\n115\t);\n116\t\n117\tCREATE INDEX idx_events_aggregate ON domain_events(aggregate_type, aggregate_id, occurred_at);\n118\tCREATE INDEX idx_events_unpublished ON domain_events(occurred_at) WHERE published_at IS NULL;\n119\t```\n120\t\n121\t## pgvector for Semantic Search (Vietnamese)\n122\t\n123\t```sql\n124\tCREATE TABLE article_embeddings (\n125\t  article_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES news_articles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n126\t  embedding vector(1536) NOT NULL,  -- OpenAI text-embedding-3-small\n127\t  model_version TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'text-embedding-3-small',\n128\t  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n129\t);\n130\t\n131\t-- HNSW index for cosine similarity search\n132\tCREATE INDEX idx_article_embeddings_hnsw ON article_embeddings \n133\t  USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops)\n134\t  WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64);\n135\t```\n136\t\n137\tSemantic search query:\n138\t```sql\n139\tSELECT \n140\t  ae.article_id,\n141\t  1 - (ae.embedding <=> $1::vector) AS similarity\n142\tFROM article_embeddings ae\n143\tWHERE 1 - (ae.embedding <=> $1::vector) > 0.85\n144\tORDER BY ae.embedding <=> $1::vector\n145\tLIMIT 10;\n146\t```\n147\t\n148\t## TimescaleDB for Price/Sentiment Time-Series\n149\t\n150\t```sql\n151\t-- Market data hypertable\n152\tCREATE TABLE market_bars (\n153\t  time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n154\t  ticker TEXT NOT NULL,\n155\t  open NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,\n156\t  high NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,\n157\t  low NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,\n158\t  close NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,\n159\t  volume BIGINT NOT NULL,\n160\t  foreign_buy_volume BIGINT,\n161\t  foreign_sell_volume BIGINT\n162\t);\n163\t\n164\tSELECT create_hypertable('market_bars', 'time');\n165\t\n166\tCREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_market_bars_ticker_time ON market_bars(ticker, time DESC);\n167\t\n168\t-- Continuous aggregate for daily OHLCV\n169\tCREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW market_bars_daily\n170\tWITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS\n171\tSELECT\n172\t  time_bucket('1 day', time) AS day,\n173\t  ticker,\n174\t  FIRST(open, time) AS open,\n175\t  MAX(high) AS high,\n176\t  MIN(low) AS low,\n177\t  LAST(close, time) AS close,\n178\t  SUM(volume) AS volume\n179\tFROM market_bars\n180\tGROUP BY day, ticker;\n181\t```\n182\t\n183\t## JSONB vs Structured Columns\n184\t\n185\t**Use structured columns when**:\n186\t- Field is queried in WHERE clauses\n187\t- Field is indexed\n188\t- Field has constraints (CHECK, NOT NULL, FK)\n189\t- Field is critical business state (ticker, dates, amounts)\n190\t\n191\t**Use JSONB when**:\n192\t- Flexible schema (different shapes per row)\n193\t- Archive / audit data\n194\t- Full document is usually returned together\n195\t- No indexed access needed on sub-fields\n196\t\n197\t## Migration Conventions\n198\t\n199\t### File Naming\n200\t`apps/api/migrations/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql`\n201\t\n202\tExample: `20260420100000_create_theses_table.sql`\n203\t\n204\t### Structure\n205\t```sql\n206\t-- Up migration\n207\tBEGIN;\n208\t\n209\tCREATE TABLE theses (/* ... */);\n210\tCREATE INDEX /* ... */;\n211\t\n212\tCOMMIT;\n213\t\n214\t-- Down migration (in comment or separate file)\n215\t-- BEGIN;\n216\t-- DROP TABLE theses;\n217\t-- COMMIT;\n218\t```\n219\t\n220\t### Rules\n221\t- Always wrap in BEGIN/COMMIT\n222\t- Idempotent where possible (`IF NOT EXISTS`)\n223\t- No data manipulation in schema migrations (use separate data migration)\n224\t- Test up and down\n225\t- One logical change per migration\n226\t\n227\t## Query Patterns\n228\t\n229\t### With explicit column list\n230\t```python\n231\t# Good\n232\trows = await db.fetch(\"\"\"\n233\t    SELECT id, status, created_at\n234\t    FROM theses\n235\t    WHERE ticker = $1 AND status = 'active'\n236\t    ORDER BY created_at DESC\n237\t\"\"\", ticker)\n238\t\n239\t# Bad — SELECT *\n240\t# rows = await db.fetch(\"SELECT * FROM theses WHERE ...\")\n241\t```\n242\t\n243\t### Prepared statements postgres-pgvector\ndescription: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n---\n\n# Skill: Postgres + pgvector + TimescaleDB\n\n## Purpose\n\nConsistent schema patterns leveraging Postgres 16 extensions for Vietnamese stock market data.\n\n## Extensions Used\n\n```sql\nCREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS \"uuid-ossp\";    -- UUID generation\nCREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS \"pg_trgm\";      -- Fuzzy text search (Vietnamese)\nCREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS \"vector\";       -- pgvector for embeddings\nCREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS \"timescaledb\";  -- Time-series (prices, sentiment)\n```\n\n## Table Design Patterns\n\n### Aggregate Root Table\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE theses (\n  -- Identity\n  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),\n  \n  -- References\n  ticker TEXT NOT NULL,\n  user_id UUID NOT NULL,\n  \n  -- State\n  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'active', 'closed')),\n  \n  -- Business content (JSONB for flexible structure)\n  bull_case JSONB NOT NULL,\n  bear_case JSONB NOT NULL,\n  catalysts JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',\n  \n  -- Calibration\n  confidence_score NUMERIC(4,3) CHECK (confidence_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1),\n  hit_rate_basis INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- N past theses of this type\n  \n  -- Temporal\n  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  submitted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,\n  closed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,\n  \n  -- Audit\n  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1  -- optimistic locking\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX idx_theses_ticker ON theses(ticker, created_at DESC);\nCREATE INDEX idx_theses_status ON theses(status) WHERE status IN ('draft', 'active');\n```\n\n### Point-in-Time Integrity (Fundamentals)\n\nEvery fundamental data row MUST have both dates:\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE financial_statements (\n  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),\n  ticker TEXT NOT NULL,\n  \n  -- CRITICAL: point-in-time integrity (I-S2)\n  period_end DATE NOT NULL,      -- what period this covers\n  filing_date DATE NOT NULL,     -- when it became public knowledge\n  \n  -- Financials (all in VND million)\n  revenue BIGINT,\n  net_income BIGINT,\n  total_assets BIGINT,\n  total_equity BIGINT,\n  \n  -- Source\n  source TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('vnstock', 'fiinpro', 'manual')),\n  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  \n  UNIQUE(ticker, period_end, filing_date, source)\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX idx_financial_ticker_period ON financial_statements(ticker, filing_date DESC, period_end DESC);\n```\n\nBacktest query MUST use filing_date filter:\n```sql\n-- CORRECT: filters by when data was known (avoids look-ahead bias)\nSELECT * FROM financial_statements\nWHERE ticker = 'VCB'\n  AND filing_date <= '2024-03-31'::date\nORDER BY period_end DESC\nLIMIT 1;\n\n-- WRONG: would introduce look-ahead bias in backtest\n-- SELECT * FROM financial_statements WHERE ticker = 'VCB' ORDER BY period_end DESC LIMIT 1;\n```\n\n### Event Log Table\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE domain_events (\n  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),\n  aggregate_id UUID NOT NULL,\n  aggregate_type TEXT NOT NULL,\n  event_type TEXT NOT NULL,\n  event_version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n  payload JSONB NOT NULL,\n  occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n  published_at TIMESTAMPTZ,\n  sequence_num BIGSERIAL NOT NULL\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX idx_events_aggregate ON domain_events(aggregate_type, aggregate_id, occurred_at);\nCREATE INDEX idx_events_unpublished ON domain_events(occurred_at) WHERE published_at IS NULL;\n```\n\n## pgvector for Semantic Search (Vietnamese)\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE article_embeddings (\n  article_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES news_articles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  embedding vector(1536) NOT NULL,  -- OpenAI text-embedding-3-small\n  model_version TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'text-embedding-3-small',\n  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- HNSW index for cosine similarity search\nCREATE INDEX idx_article_embeddings_hnsw ON article_embeddings \n  USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops)\n  WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64);\n```\n\nSemantic search query:\n```sql\nSELECT \n  ae.article_id,\n  1 - (ae.embedding <=> $1::vector) AS similarity\nFROM article_embeddings ae\nWHERE 1 - (ae.embedding <=> $1::vector) > 0.85\nORDER BY ae.embedding <=> $1::vector\nLIMIT 10;\n```\n\n## TimescaleDB for Price/Sentiment Time-Series\n\n```sql\n-- Market data hypertable\nCREATE TABLE market_bars (\n  time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n  ticker TEXT NOT NULL,\n  open NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,\n  high NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,\n  low NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,\n  close NUMERIC(15,2) NOT NULL,\n  volume BIGINT NOT NULL,\n  foreign_buy_volume BIGINT,\n  foreign_sell_volume BIGINT\n);\n\nSELECT create_hypertable('market_bars', 'time');\n\nCREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_market_bars_ticker_time ON market_bars(ticker, time DESC);\n\n-- Continuous aggregate for daily OHLCV\nCREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW market_bars_daily\nWITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS\nSELECT\n  time_bucket('1 day', time) AS day,\n  ticker,\n  FIRST(open, time) AS open,\n  MAX(high) AS high,\n  MIN(low) AS low,\n  LAST(close, time) AS close,\n  SUM(volume) AS volume\nFROM market_bars\nGROUP BY day, ticker;\n```\n\n## JSONB vs Structured Columns\n\n**Use structured columns when**:\n- Field is queried in WHERE clauses\n- Field is indexed\n- Field has constraints (CHECK, NOT NULL, FK)\n- Field is critical business state (ticker, dates, amounts)\n\n**Use JSONB when**:\n- Flexible schema (different shapes per row)\n- Archive / audit data\n- Full document is usually returned together\n- No indexed access needed on sub-fields\n\n## Migration Conventions\n\n### File Naming\n`apps/api/migrations/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql`\n\nExample: `20260420100000_create_theses_table.sql`\n\n### Structure\n```sql\n-- Up migration\nBEGIN;\n\nCREATE TABLE theses (/* ... */);\nCREATE INDEX /* ... */;\n\nCOMMIT;\n\n-- Down migration (in comment or separate file)\n-- BEGIN;\n-- DROP TABLE theses;\n-- COMMIT;\n```\n\n### Rules\n- Always wrap in BEGIN/COMMIT\n- Idempotent where possible (`IF NOT EXISTS`)\n- No data manipulation in schema migrations (use separate data migration)\n- Test up and down\n- One logical change per migration\n\n## Query Patterns\n\n### With explicit column list\n```python\n# Good\nrows = await db.fetch(\"\"\"\n    SELECT id, status, created_at\n    FROM theses\n    WHERE ticker = $1 AND status = 'active'\n    ORDER BY created_at DESC\n\"\"\", ticker)\n\n# Bad — SELECT *\n# rows = await db.fetch(\"SELECT * FROM theses WHERE ...\")\n```\n\n### Prepared statements (asyncpg)\n```python\n# Use parameterized queries always\nstmt = await conn.prepare(\"SELECT * FROM theses WHERE id = $1\")\nrow = await stmt.fetchrow(thesis_id)\n\n# Never string interpolation\n# await conn.fetch(f\"SELECT * FROM theses WHERE id = '{thesis_id}'\")  # SQL INJECTION\n```\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Put business logic in triggers (use application)\n- Use `SELECT *` in production code\n- Skip migrations for \"quick schema change\"\n- Index everything \"just in case\" (slows writes)\n- Store timestamps without TZ (always use TIMESTAMPTZ)\n- Use JSONB for queryable fields (ticker, dates, status)\n- Query fundamental data without filing_date filter in backtest paths (I-S2 violation)\n\n**Do**:\n- Structured columns for queryable fields\n- JSONB for flexible/archival metadata\n- HNSW index for pgvector\n- Prepared statements always\n- Transactions for multi-statement logic\n- Version tracking with `version` column for optimistic locking\n- TIMESTAMPTZ for all timestamps\n\n## Related\n\n- `ddd-tactical-patterns` — aggregates mapped to these tables\n- `fastapi-module` — repositories accessing these tables (Phase 2+)\n","numLines":277,"startLine":1,"totalLines":277}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"6cb4ecfc-4dd3-4c9d-9976-94c4687ffbe6","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

Hidden Assumptions**\n49\t- What must be true for this to work?\n50\t- Which of those are unverified?\n51\t- Which could silently be false?\n52\t\n53\t**B. Edge Cases**\n54\t- What inputs break this?\n55\t- What conditions weren't considered?\n56\t- What happens at scale boundaries (0, 1, 10K, 1M)?\n57\t\n58\t**C. Failure Modes**\n59\t- What's the blast radius when this fails?\n60\t- How do we detect failure?\n61\t- How long to recover?\n62\t- Partial failures handled?\n63\t\n64\t**D. Alternative Paths**\n65\t- Is there a simpler way?\n66\t- Is there a more robust way?\n67\t- Is there a cheaper way?\n68\t- What would a quant fund do differently?\n69\t\n70\t**E. Historical Parallel**\n71\t- Has this been tried before (by others)?\n72\t- What happened?\n73\t- Why do we think our outcome will be different?\n74\t\n75\t**F. Incentive Misalignment**\n76\t- Does this create wrong incentives anywhere?\n77\t- Who benefits? Who pays?\n78\t- Does success create new problems?\n79\t\n80\t**G. Second-Order Effects**\n81\t- If this succeeds, what changes downstream?\n82\t- Which changes are intended?\n83\t- Which might be unwelcome?\n84\t\n85\t**H. Specific to StockForge**\n86\t- No LLM math violated? Numbers traced to code with verified inputs?\n87\t- Citation integrity maintained? Every claim has source + as-of date?\n88\t- Bear case present and substantive? (Single-perspective = anti-pattern)\n89\t- Calibration: any confidence claims without historical hit rate support?\n90\t- Does this respect Clean Architecture? (Domain pure, no Pydantic in domain)\n91\t- Output framed as research aid, not financial advice?\n92\t- Insider information risk? (Public sources only)\n93\t\n94\t### 4. Subagent Output Format\n95\t\n96\t```markdown\n97\t# Devil's Advocate Critique — [target]\n98\t\n99\t## Target Under Review\n100\t[Brief description of what's being critiqued]\n101\t\n102\t## Overall Verdict\n103\t[STRONG | ACCEPTABLE WITH CONCERNS | SIGNIFICANT CONCERNS | SHOULD RECONSIDER]\n104\t\n105\t## Hidden Assumptions Found\n106\t1. **Assumption**: [what's being assumed]\n107\t   **Risk if wrong**: [consequence]\n108\t   **Verification**: [how to check]\n109\t\n110\t2. ...\n111\t\n112\t## Edge Cases Not Handled\n113\t1. **Case**: [specific scenario]\n114\t   **Expected behavior**: [what should happen]\n115\t   **Current behavior**: [likely unhandled]\n116\t   **Severity**: HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW\n117\t\n118\t2. ...\n119\t\n120\t## Failure Mode Analysis\n121\t- **Most likely failure**: [description]\n122\t- **Detection time**: [estimate]\n123\t- **Blast radius**: [scope of damage]\n124\t- **Recovery path**: [how to restore]\n125\t- **Gaps in recovery**: [what's missing]\n126\t\n127\t## Alternatives Worth Considering\n128\t1. **Alternative A**: [description]\n129\t   - Pro: [advantages]\n130\t   - Con: [disadvantages]\n131\t   - Why not chosen in current approach: [best guess]\n132\t\n133\t2. ...\n134\t\n135\t## Historical Precedents\n136\t- [Fund/project X] tried [similar thing] in [year], result: [outcome]\n137\t- [Pattern Y] commonly fails because [reason]\n138\t\n139\t## Second-Order Concerns\n140\t- If this works, [downstream consequence]\n141\t- Intended: [beneficial]\n142\t- Unintended: [concerning]\n143\t\n144\t## StockForge-Specific Risks\n145\t- No-LLM-math: [respected / at risk]\n146\t- Citation integrity: [maintained / gaps: list]\n147\t- Bear case: [present and substantive / missing / superficial]\n148\t- Confidence calibrated: [to hit rate / uncalibrated claim]\n149\t- Architecture: [clean / violations: list]\n150\t- Framing: [research aid / sliding toward advice]\n151\t\n152\t## Top 3 Issues to Address\n153\t\n154\t### Issue 1: [short name]\n155\t**Severity**: HIGH\n156\t**Problem**: [description]\n157\t**Suggested fix**: [concrete suggestion]\n158\t\n159\t### Issue 2: [short name]\n160\t**Severity**: MEDIUM\n161\t...\n162\t\n163\t### Issue 3: [short name]\n164\t**Severity**: MEDIUM\n165\t...\n166\t\n167\t## Strengths (to preserve while fixing issues)\n168\t1. [Genuinely strong aspect]\n169\t2. [Another strength]\n170\t\n171\t## Recommendation\n172\t[STOP AND REDESIGN | ADJUST AND PROCEED | PROCEED WITH CAUTION | PROCEED AS PLANNED]\n173\t\n174\tSpecific action: [what to do next]\n175\t```\n176\t\n177\t### 5. Present Critique to User\n178\t\n179\tDon't just forward raw subagent output. Add:\n180\t\n181\t```markdown\n182\t# Devil's Advocate Found [N] Concerns\n183\t\n184\t## Summary\n185\t[2-3 sentence honest summary]\n186\t\n187\t## Must Address (before proceeding)\n188\t- [Issue 1 from HIGH severity]\n189\t- [Issue 2 from HIGH severity]\n190\t\n191\t## Should Consider\n192\t- [Medium severity issues worth thinking about]\n193\t\n194\t## Might Be OK\n195\t- [Lower severity, noted for awareness]\n196\t\n197\t[Full critique]\n198\t\n199\t## Your Call\n200\tGiven this critique:\n201\t- Address high-severity issues?\n202\t- Accept and proceed (document rationale)?\n203\t- Reconsider the approach?\n204\t```\n205\t\n206\t### 6. Handle Response\n207\t\n208\tUser may:\n209\t- Accept critique and adjust → good, iterate\n210\t- Accept critique but proceed anyway → document rationale in `agent-notes.md`\n211\t- Reject critique → document why in same file\n212\t\n213\tImportant: critique is input, not mandate. User decides.\n214\t\n215\t---\n216\t\n217\t## When to Override Critique\n218\t\n219\tSometimes devils-advocate finds theoretical problems that don't matter in practice:\n220\t- Edge case at scale we'll never hit\n221\t- Failure mode mitigated by other mechanism\n222\t- \"What if\" concern not worth addressing preemptively\n223\t\n224\tIn those cases, document in revisit**: [what would change our mind]\n231\t```\n232\t\n233\tThis creates institutional memory — if the concern becomes real later, we know we saw it coming.\n234\t\n235\t---\n236\t\n237\t## Subagent Output Format\n\n```markdown\n# Devil's Advocate Critique — [target]\n\n## Target Under Review\n[Brief description of what's being critiqued]\n\n## Overall Verdict\n[STRONG | ACCEPTABLE WITH CONCERNS | SIGNIFICANT CONCERNS | SHOULD RECONSIDER]\n\n## Hidden Assumptions Found\n1. **Assumption**: [what's being assumed]\n   **Risk if wrong**: [consequence]\n   **Verification**: [how to check]\n\n2. ...\n\n## Edge Cases Not Handled\n1. **Case**: [specific scenario]\n   **Expected behavior**: [what should happen]\n   **Current behavior**: [likely unhandled]\n   **Severity**: HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW\n\n2. ...\n\n## Failure Mode Analysis\n- **Most likely failure**: [description]\n- **Detection time**: [estimate]\n- **Blast radius**: [scope of damage]\n- **Recovery path**: [how to restore]\n- **Gaps in recovery**: [what's missing]\n\n## Alternatives Worth Considering\n1. **Alternative A**: [description]\n   - Pro: [advantages]\n   - Con: [disadvantages]\n   - Why not chosen in current approach: [best guess]\n\n2. ...\n\n## Historical Precedents\n- [Fund/project X] tried [similar thing] in [year], result: [outcome]\n- [Pattern Y] commonly fails because [reason]\n\n## Second-Order Concerns\n- If this works, [downstream consequence]\n- Intended: [beneficial]\n- Unintended: [concerning]\n\n## StockForge-Specific Risks\n- No-LLM-math: [respected / at risk]\n- Citation integrity: [maintained / gaps: list]\n- Bear case: [present and substantive / missing / superficial]\n- Confidence calibrated: [to hit rate / uncalibrated claim]\n- Architecture: [clean / violations: list]\n- Framing: [research aid / sliding toward advice]\n\n## Top 3 Issues to Address\n\n### Issue 1: [short name]\n**Severity**: HIGH\n**Problem**: [description]\n**Suggested fix**: [concrete suggestion]\n\n### Issue 2: [short name]\n**Severity**: MEDIUM\n...\n\n### Issue 3: [short name]\n**Severity**: MEDIUM\n...\n\n## Strengths (to preserve while fixing issues)\n1. [Genuinely strong aspect]\n2. [Another strength]\n\n## Recommendation\n[STOP AND REDESIGN | ADJUST AND PROCEED | PROCEED WITH CAUTION | PROCEED AS PLANNED]\n\nSpecific action: [what to do next]\n```\n\n### 5. Present Critique to User\n\nDon't just forward raw subagent output. Add:\n\n```markdown\n# Devil's Advocate Found [N] Concerns\n\n## Summary\n[2-3 sentence honest summary]\n\n## Must Address (before proceeding)\n- [Issue 1 from HIGH severity]\n- [Issue 2 from HIGH severity]\n\n## Should Consider\n- [Medium severity issues worth thinking about]\n\n## Might Be OK\n- [Lower severity, noted for awareness]\n\n[Full critique]\n\n## Your Call\nGiven this critique:\n- Address high-severity issues?\n- Accept and proceed (document rationale)?\n- Reconsider the approach?\n```\n\n### 6. Handle Response\n\nUser may:\n- Accept critique and adjust → good, iterate\n- Accept critique but proceed anyway → document rationale in `agent-notes.md`\n- Reject critique → document why in same file\n\nImportant: critique is input, not mandate. User decides.\n\n---\n\n## When to Override Critique\n\nSometimes devils-advocate finds theoretical problems that don't matter in practice:\n- Edge case at scale we'll never hit\n- Failure mode mitigated by other mechanism\n- \"What if\" concern not worth addressing preemptively\n\nIn those cases, document in `agent-notes.md`:\n```markdown\n## YYYY-MM-DD — Devils Advocate Override — [target]\n\n**Concern raised**: [what]\n**Why overridden**: [reason]\n**Conditions to revisit**: [what would change our mind]\n```\n\nThis creates institutional memory — if the concern becomes real later, we know we saw it coming.\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Skip this for \"obvious\" decisions (those are often the most wrong)\n- Use this as a second opinion when you want validation (it's designed to disagree)\n- Dismiss critique as \"not understanding our context\" (could be true, could be denial)\n- Run this and ignore output (waste of tokens)\n- Skip the StockForge-specific checks (they exist because finance + LLM = real money risk)\n\n**Do**:\n- Run on major decisions and thesis outputs\n- Take critique seriously even when uncomfortable\n- Document override rationale when proceeding anyway\n- Use for adversarial rehearsal before acting on investment decisions\n","numLines":251,"startLine":1,"totalLines":251}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f36d5cda-7fb6-4b5f-9c1e-c2f3ccc4a59e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}
