{"parentUuid":"bbce2a03-d713-46f3-aeba-39c20fa747e6","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01NFi5j62uU8kFVyuqw2fxjA","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_018CvWaXdbAj6g3aRnCk4Frh","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\test-pyramid-balance\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: test-pyramid-balance\ndescription: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\nallowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash]\n---\n\n# Skill: Test Pyramid Balance\n\n## Purpose\n\nNot all tests are equal. Wrong mix = slow suite, fragile tests, or false confidence. Encodes the layer decisions + stock-domain-specific test categories that prevent the most expensive mistake (testing LLM output content + LLM-computed numbers).\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Deciding what test to write for a new feature\n- Reviewing PR test coverage\n- Rebalancing a skewed suite (red flags below)\n- Authoring a thesis/extractor module — what counts as testable?\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Test-free prototype scripts (Phase 1 spike code)\n- Pure UI snapshot tests for Streamlit dashboards (visual regression is its own discipline)\n\n## The Pyramid\n\n```\n          /\\\n         /E2E\\        Few (~10-20 in MVP)\n        /------\\      Slow, expensive, flaky\n       /Integra-\\     Some (~100-300)\n      / tion    \\     Medium speed, real systems\n     /------------\\\n    /    Unit      \\  Many (~1000+)\n   /----------------\\ Fast, focused, numerous\n```\n\n## Test Layer Decision Table\n\n| Layer | Target | Speed | Deps | Use for |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Unit** (`packages/*/tests/`) | Pure domain logic, VOs, services | <10ms | None | Business rules, value object constraints, state transitions, edge cases in domain |\n| **Integration** (`apps/*/tests/`, `packages/*/tests/integration/`) | Use cases + adapters | <500ms | Real DB (testcontainers), Redis; mocked external APIs | Repository implementations, event publish/subscribe, queries (incl. point-in-time integrity) |\n| **E2E / BDD** (`bdd/features/*.feature`) | Critical user journeys | seconds | Full stack | Happy path of core features, cross-component workflows |\n\nSee `references/test-examples.md` for ready-to-paste pytest + gherkin templates.\n\n## Stock-Specific Test Categories\n\n### Domain Tests (`pytest packages/domain/`)\nPure logic, no LLM, no DB. Validate value object invariants (Ticker, Money, Period), aggregate invariants (Thesis requires bear case), state transitions.\n\n### Backtest Tests (`pytest tests/backtest/`)\nReplay historical data; verify decisions. **MUST verify point-in-time integrity** — backtest paths use `filing_date <= as_of` filter (I-S2). Never use \"latest\" fundamental data.\n\n### LLM Extractor Snapshot Tests\nTest **structure**, not LLM creativity. Assert that every extracted claim has `source_url`, `extracted_at`, `confidence ∈ [0,1]`. Do NOT assert on specific LLM phrasing — too fragile, and assertions on LLM-generated numbers would violate I-S1.\n\n### Calibration Tests\nGiven known historical outcomes, score functions should converge. Asserts `0.65 ≤ kol.credibility_score ≤ 0.75` for 7/10 hits, etc. Used to detect calibration drift.\n\n## The 70-20-10 Guideline\n\nFor a mature codebase:\n- **70% unit** — fast, numerous, cover domain logic\n- **20% integration** — verify adapters work\n- **10% E2E/BDD** — critical flows end-to-end\n\nIn MVP: closer to 50-40-10 may be acceptable. But don't let integration tests dominate — they're slow and brittle.\n\n## Coverage Targets\n\n- **Domain layer** (`packages/domain/`) — 100% unit coverage. Nothing touches IO; no excuse.\n- **Application layer** (`packages/application/`) — 80% integration coverage. Use cases tested end-to-end with real DB.\n- **Infrastructure** (`packages/infrastructure/`) — adapter contract tests. Each adapter has integration test verifying it meets Protocol.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n### Don't test LLM-generated text content\nAsserting `\"NPL\" in result.bear_case` is fragile — LLM might phrase it differently. Test the **domain invariant** instead: `thesis.bear_case.is_substantive()`.\n\n### Don't test LLM math (it shouldn't exist)\nA test like `assert result.pe_ratio == 12.5` after `llm.analyze(...)` is a charter violation (I-S1). Code computes; LLM only interprets. Test the code: `assert compute_pe(price, eps) == pytest.approx(12.5)`.\n\n### Don't invert the pyramid\nIntegration tests > unit tests in count = ice-cream cone, not pyramid. Slow, brittle, hides domain bugs.\n\n### Don't skip BDD for top user flows\nIf the top 3 user flows aren't covered by BDD scenarios, the team can't refactor with confidence.\n\n### Don't smear domain rules across integration tests\nIf domain invariants are only verified through DB-backed integration tests, debugging is slow + the unit layer is empty (red flag).\n\n## Detecting Imbalance — Red Flags\n\n- Integration tests > unit tests in count (inverted pyramid)\n- Unit-layer suite > 5 min (too many slow tests at unit layer)\n- E2E > 20% of tests (expensive, brittle)\n- No BDD scenarios for top 3 user flows\n- Domain rules only verified through integration tests (slow, hard to debug)\n- Tests asserting on LLM-generated text content or LLM-computed numbers (fragile, charter violation)\n\n## Validation Pre-Conditions\n\n- Suite distribution within ~70/20/10 (or trending toward it)\n- Domain layer has 100% unit coverage; no integration test substitutes for missing unit coverage\n- Backtest paths filter on `filing_date` (grep — `Grep \"filing_date\" tests/backtest/`)\n- LLM extractor tests assert on structure (`source_url`, `extracted_at`), NOT on text content\n\n## Smoke Test\n\nFor task \"thesis-validation use case has integration coverage\":\n\nExpected output:\n- 1 integration test in `apps/api/tests/test_validate_thesis_integration.py` that uses real Postgres via testcontainers + mocks event bus\n- Test asserts: persistence (`from_db.status == ThesisStatus.ACTIVE`), event emitted (`ThesisCreated` in published_events)\n- Domain invariants (substantive bear case) tested separately as **unit** tests in `packages/domain/analysis/tests/test_thesis.py`\n\nIf proposal places domain-invariant tests in unit layer + use-case-with-DB in integration layer + BDD for the user-facing flow → pyramid is balanced.\n\n## See Also\n\n- `references/test-examples.md` — full pytest + gherkin templates (unit, integration, BDD, snapshot, calibration, anti-pattern)\n- `spec-dual-layer` SKILL.md § B.9 — test requirements section in specs\n- `ddd-tactical-patterns` SKILL.md — what's worth unit testing\n- `fastapi-module` SKILL.md — integration test setup (Phase 2+)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8535,"cache_read_input_tokens":208914,"output_tokens":5058,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8535,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":5058,"cache_read_input_tokens":208914,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8535,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8535},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYEQLMdNueVeJug1JEhv","attributionSkill":"update-config","type":"assistant","uuid":"6ac8389d-ab78-402f-8273-ef7ed552cfc1","timestamp":"2026-04-29T14:37:24.809Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"6ac8389d-ab78-402f-8273-ef7ed552cfc1","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01NFi5j62uU8kFVyuqw2fxjA","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Mm3y72iu5PGhnVWmkaVJw7","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\test-pyramid-balance\\references\\test-examples.md","content":"# Test Examples — Templates by Layer\n\n> Reference companion to `../SKILL.md`. Verbatim pytest + gherkin templates.\n\n## Unit Test (Domain Logic)\n\n```python\n# packages/domain/analysis/tests/test_thesis.py\nimport pytest\nfrom packages.domain.analysis.models.thesis import Thesis, ThesisStatus\nfrom packages.domain.analysis.errors import InvariantViolation, InvalidStateError\n\ndef test_thesis_requires_substantive_bear_case() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Charter principle: adversarial by design — bear case mandatory.\"\"\"\n    with pytest.raises(InvariantViolation, match=\"bear case\"):\n        Thesis.create(\n            ticker=Ticker.from_str(\"VCB\"),\n            bull_case=BullCase(\"Strong earnings growth...\"),\n            bear_case=BearCase(\"\"),  # empty — must fail\n        )\n\ndef test_thesis_cannot_add_catalyst_when_active() -> None:\n    thesis = make_active_thesis()\n    with pytest.raises(InvalidStateError):\n        thesis.add_catalyst(make_catalyst())\n```\n\n## Integration Test (Use Case + Real DB)\n\n```python\n# apps/api/tests/test_validate_thesis_integration.py\nimport pytest\nfrom testcontainers.postgres import PostgresContainer\n\n@pytest.fixture(scope=\"session\")\ndef postgres():\n    with PostgresContainer(\"postgres:16\") as pg:\n        yield pg\n\nasync def test_validate_thesis_persists_and_emits_event(postgres, event_bus_mock):\n    repo = ThesisPostgresRepository(db=make_db(postgres))\n    use_case = ValidateThesisUseCase(thesis_repo=repo, event_bus=event_bus_mock)\n\n    result = await use_case.execute(\n        ticker=\"VCB\",\n        bull_case=\"Strong earnings growth driven by retail expansion...\",\n        bear_case=\"Rising NPL ratio may compress margins and trigger provision surge...\",\n    )\n\n    # Verify persistence\n    from_db = await repo.find_by_id(result.id)\n    assert from_db is not None\n    assert from_db.status == ThesisStatus.ACTIVE\n\n    # Verify event emitted\n    assert event_bus_mock.published_events[-1].type == \"ThesisCreated\"\n```\n\n## BDD Scenario\n\n```gherkin\n# bdd/features/validate_investment_thesis.feature\nFeature: Validate Investment Thesis\n\n  Scenario: User submits thesis with both bull and bear case\n    Given user is authenticated\n    When user submits thesis for ticker \"VCB\"\n      And bull case is \"Strong earnings growth...\"\n      And bear case is \"Rising NPL ratio may compress margins...\"\n    Then thesis status is \"active\"\n    And thesis has non-empty bear case\n    And ThesisCreated event is emitted\n```\n\n## LLM Extractor Snapshot Test\n\n```python\n# tests/snapshots/test_claim_extraction.py\ndef test_claim_extraction_vcb_article() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Snapshot test — input text → expected structured output.\n\n    We test that EVERY claim has the required structural fields.\n    We do NOT assert on specific LLM phrasing or numbers — that would\n    violate I-S1 (no LLM math) and produce a fragile test.\n    \"\"\"\n    with open(\"tests/snapshots/vcb_q1_2026_article.txt\") as f:\n        article = f.read()\n\n    result = extract_claims_from_article(article, use_cache=True)\n\n    assert all(c.source_url for c in result.claims)            # I-S1: source pointer\n    assert all(c.extracted_at for c in result.claims)          # I-S2: as-of date\n    assert all(0 <= c.confidence <= 1 for c in result.claims)  # bounded score\n    # Numbers in claims came from source text quotes, not LLM computation\n```\n\n## Calibration Test\n\n```python\n# tests/calibration/test_kol_credibility.py\ndef test_credibility_score_converges_with_outcome_data() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Given 10 past recommendations with known outcomes, score should be ~0.7.\"\"\"\n    kol = make_kol()\n    outcomes = [True, True, False, True, True, False, True, True, True, False]\n\n    for i, hit in enumerate(outcomes):\n        kol.record_recommendation_outcome(make_recommendation(i), hit)\n\n    score = kol.credibility_score\n    assert 0.65 <= score.value <= 0.75, f\"Expected ~0.7, got {score.value}\"\n```\n\n## Anti-Pattern Examples\n\n### Bad — asserting on LLM-generated text\n\n```python\ndef test_bear_case_mentions_risk():\n    result = llm_analyze_thesis(ticker=\"VCB\")\n    assert \"NPL\" in result.bear_case  # LLM might phrase it differently\n```\n\n### Good — test domain invariant\n\n```python\ndef test_thesis_has_substantive_bear_case():\n    thesis = Thesis.create(ticker, bull, bear)\n    assert thesis.bear_case.is_substantive()  # domain method, not LLM assertion\n```\n\n### Bad — testing LLM math (charter violation)\n\n```python\ndef test_llm_computes_pe_ratio():\n    result = llm.analyze(ticker=\"VCB\")\n    assert result.pe_ratio == 12.5  # WRONG: LLM should not compute ratios\n```\n\n### Good — code computes, test verifies code\n\n```python\ndef test_pe_ratio_computation():\n    pe = compute_pe(price=Money.vnd(50_000), eps=Money.vnd(4_000))\n    assert pe == pytest.approx(12.5, rel=0.01)\n```\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8535,"cache_read_input_tokens":208914,"output_tokens":5058,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8535,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":5058,"cache_read_input_tokens":208914,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8535,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8535},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYEQLMdNueVeJug1JEhv","attributionSkill":"update-config","type":"assistant","uuid":"3ad82d7a-da04-49aa-b592-7e4e21297f8d","timestamp":"2026-04-29T14:37:47.674Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"6ac8389d-ab78-402f-8273-ef7ed552cfc1","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"6e3280d2-17f5-4df9-be4d-ac8a54f7c10f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018CvWaXdbAj6g3aRnCk4Frh","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\test-pyramid-balance\\SKILL.md has been updated successfully."}]},"uuid":"4ad0008b-8efe-4327-a8eb-9110edfa4131","timestamp":"2026-04-29T14:46:53.703Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"update","filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\test-pyramid-balance\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: test-pyramid-balance\ndescription: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\nallowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash]\n---\n\n# Skill: Test Pyramid Balance\n\n## Purpose\n\nNot all tests are equal. Wrong mix = slow suite, fragile tests, or false confidence. Encodes the layer decisions + stock-domain-specific test categories that prevent the most expensive mistake (testing LLM output content + LLM-computed numbers).\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Deciding what test to write for a new feature\n- Reviewing PR test coverage\n- Rebalancing a skewed suite (red flags below)\n- Authoring a thesis/extractor module — what counts as testable?\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Test-free prototype scripts (Phase 1 spike code)\n- Pure UI snapshot tests for Streamlit dashboards (visual regression is its own discipline)\n\n## The Pyramid\n\n```\n          /\\\n         /E2E\\        Few (~10-20 in MVP)\n        /------\\      Slow, expensive, flaky\n       /Integra-\\     Some (~100-300)\n      / tion    \\     Medium speed, real systems\n     /------------\\\n    /    Unit      \\  Many (~1000+)\n   /----------------\\ Fast, focused, numerous\n```\n\n## Test Layer Decision Table\n\n| Layer | Target | Speed | Deps | Use for |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Unit** (`packages/*/tests/`) | Pure domain logic, VOs, services | <10ms | None | Business rules, value object constraints, state transitions, edge cases in domain |\n| **Integration** (`apps/*/tests/`, `packages/*/tests/integration/`) | Use cases + adapters | <500ms | Real DB (testcontainers), Redis; mocked external APIs | Repository implementations, event publish/subscribe, queries (incl. point-in-time integrity) |\n| **E2E / BDD** (`bdd/features/*.feature`) | Critical user journeys | seconds | Full stack | Happy path of core features, cross-component workflows |\n\nSee `references/test-examples.md` for ready-to-paste pytest + gherkin templates.\n\n## Stock-Specific Test Categories\n\n### Domain Tests (`pytest packages/domain/`)\nPure logic, no LLM, no DB. Validate value object invariants (Ticker, Money, Period), aggregate invariants (Thesis requires bear case), state transitions.\n\n### Backtest Tests (`pytest tests/backtest/`)\nReplay historical data; verify decisions. **MUST verify point-in-time integrity** — backtest paths use `filing_date <= as_of` filter (I-S2). Never use \"latest\" fundamental data.\n\n### LLM Extractor Snapshot Tests\nTest **structure**, not LLM creativity. Assert that every extracted claim has `source_url`, `extracted_at`, `confidence ∈ [0,1]`. Do NOT assert on specific LLM phrasing — too fragile, and assertions on LLM-generated numbers would violate I-S1.\n\n### Calibration Tests\nGiven known historical outcomes, score functions should converge. Asserts `0.65 ≤ kol.credibility_score ≤ 0.75` for 7/10 hits, etc. Used to detect calibration drift.\n\n## The 70-20-10 Guideline\n\nFor a mature codebase:\n- **70% unit** — fast, numerous, cover domain logic\n- **20% integration** — verify adapters work\n- **10% E2E/BDD** — critical flows end-to-end\n\nIn MVP: closer to 50-40-10 may be acceptable. But don't let integration tests dominate — they're slow and brittle.\n\n## Coverage Targets\n\n- **Domain layer** (`packages/domain/`) — 100% unit coverage. Nothing touches IO; no excuse.\n- **Application layer** (`packages/application/`) — 80% integration coverage. Use cases tested end-to-end with real DB.\n- **Infrastructure** (`packages/infrastructure/`) — adapter contract tests. Each adapter has integration test verifying it meets Protocol.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n### Don't test LLM-generated text content\nAsserting `\"NPL\" in result.bear_case` is fragile — LLM might phrase it differently. Test the **domain invariant** instead: `thesis.bear_case.is_substantive()`.\n\n### Don't test LLM math (it shouldn't exist)\nA test like `assert result.pe_ratio == 12.5` after `llm.analyze(...)` is a charter violation (I-S1). Code computes; LLM only interprets. Test the code: `assert compute_pe(price, eps) == pytest.approx(12.5)`.\n\n### Don't invert the pyramid\nIntegration tests > unit tests in count = ice-cream cone, not pyramid. Slow, brittle, hides domain bugs.\n\n### Don't skip BDD for top user flows\nIf the top 3 user flows aren't covered by BDD scenarios, the team can't refactor with confidence.\n\n### Don't smear domain rules across integration tests\nIf domain invariants are only verified through DB-backed integration tests, debugging is slow + the unit layer is empty (red flag).\n\n## Detecting Imbalance — Red Flags\n\n- Integration tests > unit tests in count (inverted pyramid)\n- Unit-layer suite > 5 min (too many slow tests at unit layer)\n- E2E > 20% of tests (expensive, brittle)\n- No BDD scenarios for top 3 user flows\n- Domain rules only verified through integration tests (slow, hard to debug)\n- Tests asserting on LLM-generated text content or LLM-computed numbers (fragile, charter violation)\n\n## Validation Pre-Conditions\n\n- Suite distribution within ~70/20/10 (or trending toward it)\n- Domain layer has 100% unit coverage; no integration test substitutes for missing unit coverage\n- Backtest paths filter on `filing_date` (grep — `Grep \"filing_date\" tests/backtest/`)\n- LLM extractor tests assert on structure (`source_url`, `extracted_at`), NOT on text content\n\n## Smoke Test\n\nFor task \"thesis-validation use case has integration coverage\":\n\nExpected output:\n- 1 integration test in `apps/api/tests/test_validate_thesis_integration.py` that uses real Postgres via testcontainers + mocks event bus\n- Test asserts: persistence (`from_db.status == ThesisStatus.ACTIVE`), event emitted (`ThesisCreated` in published_events)\n- Domain invariants (substantive bear case) tested separately as **unit** tests in `packages/domain/analysis/tests/test_thesis.py`\n\nIf proposal places domain-invariant tests in unit layer + use-case-with-DB in integration layer + BDD for the user-facing flow → pyramid is balanced.\n\n## See Also\n\n- `references/test-examples.md` — full pytest + gherkin templates (unit, integration, BDD, snapshot, calibration, anti-pattern)\n- `spec-dual-layer` SKILL.md § B.9 — test requirements section in specs\n- `ddd-tactical-patterns` SKILL.md — what's worth unit testing\n- `fastapi-module` SKILL.md — integration test setup (Phase 2+)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":14,"newStart":1,"newLines":27,"lines":[" ---"," name: test-pyramid-balance"," description: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. 2+)"]}],"originalFile":"---\nname: test-pyramid-balance\ndescription: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n---\n\n# Skill: Test Pyramid Balance\n\n## Purpose\n\nNot all tests are equal. Wrong mix = slow suite, fragile tests, or false confidence.\n\n## The Pyramid\n\n```\n          /\\\n         /E2E\\        Few (~10-20 in MVP)\n        /------\\      Slow, expensive, flaky\n       /Integra-\\     Some (~100-300)\n      / tion    \\     Medium speed, real systems\n     /------------\\\n    /    Unit      \\  Many (~1000+)\n   /----------------\\ Fast, focused, numerous\n```\n\n## Test Types — When to Use\n\n### Unit Tests\n**Target**: Pure domain logic, value objects, domain services.\n**Location**: Co-located `test_*.py` next to source, or `tests/unit/`.\n**Speed**: < 10ms each.\n**Dependencies**: None (no DB, no API, no file IO).\n\n**Use for**:\n- Business rule validation (`Thesis.submit()` behavior)\n- Value object constraints (`Ticker.from_str('invalid')`)\n- Domain services (valuation formulas — BUT computed by deterministic code, not tested for LLM output)\n- Edge cases in domain logic\n\n**Example**:\n```python\n# packages/domain/analysis/tests/test_thesis.py\nimport pytest\nfrom packages.domain.analysis.models.thesis import Thesis, ThesisStatus\nfrom packages.domain.analysis.errors import InvariantViolation, InvalidStateError\n\ndef test_thesis_requires_substantive_bear_case() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Charter principle: adversarial by design — bear case mandatory.\"\"\"\n    with pytest.raises(InvariantViolation, match=\"bear case\"):\n        Thesis.create(\n            ticker=Ticker.from_str(\"VCB\"),\n            bull_case=BullCase(\"Strong earnings growth...\"),\n            bear_case=BearCase(\"\"),  # empty — must fail\n        )\n\ndef test_thesis_cannot_add_catalyst_when_active() -> None:\n    thesis = make_active_thesis()\n    with pytest.raises(InvalidStateError):\n        thesis.add_catalyst(make_catalyst())\n```\n\n### Integration Tests\n**Target**: Use cases + adapters, module boundaries.\n**Location**: `apps/*/tests/` or `packages/*/tests/integration/`.\n**Speed**: < 500ms each typically.\n**Dependencies**: Real DB (pytest + testcontainers), real Redis, mocked external APIs.\n\n**Use for**:\n- Use case end-to-end with real persistence\n- Repository implementations\n- Event publishing + subscribing\n- Database queries (including point-in-time integrity)\n\n**Example**:\n```python\n# apps/api/tests/test_validate_thesis_integration.py\nimport pytest\nfrom testcontainers.postgres import PostgresContainer\n\n@pytest.fixture(scope=\"session\")\ndef postgres():\n    with PostgresContainer(\"postgres:16\") as pg:\n        yield pg\n\nasync def test_validate_thesis_persists_and_emits_event(postgres, event_bus_mock):\n    repo = ThesisPostgresRepository(db=make_db(postgres))\n    use_case = ValidateThesisUseCase(thesis_repo=repo, event_bus=event_bus_mock)\n    \n    result = await use_case.execute(\n        ticker=\"VCB\",\n        bull_case=\"Strong earnings growth driven by retail expansion...\",\n        bear_case=\"Rising NPL ratio may compress margins and trigger provision surge...\",\n    )\n    \n    # Verify persistence\n    from_db = await repo.find_by_id(result.id)\n    assert from_db is not None\n    assert from_db.status == ThesisStatus.ACTIVE\n    \n    # Verify event emitted\n    assert event_bus_mock.published_events[-1].type == \"ThesisCreated\"\n```\n\n### E2E / BDD Tests\n**Target**: Critical user journeys.\n**Location**: `bdd/features/*.feature` + Python step definitions.\n**Speed**: seconds per test.\n**Dependencies**: Full stack running.\n\n**Use for**:\n- Happy path of core features\n- Critical business flows\n- Cross-component workflows\n\n**Example**:\n```gherkin\n# bdd/features/validate_investment_thesis.feature\nFeature: Validate Investment Thesis\n\n  Scenario: User submits thesis with both bull and bear case\n    Given user is authenticated\n    When user submits thesis for ticker \"VCB\"\n      And bull case is \"Strong earnings growth...\"\n      And bear case is \"Rising NPL ratio may compress margins...\"\n    Then thesis status is \"active\"\n    And thesis has non-empty bear case\n    And ThesisCreated event is emitted\n```\n\n## Stock-Specific Test Categories\n\n### Domain Tests (`pytest packages/domain/`)\n- Pure logic, no LLM, no DB\n- Validate: value object invariants (Ticker, Money, Period)\n- Validate: aggregate invariants (Thesis requires bear case)\n- Validate: state transitions\n\n### Backtest Tests (`pytest tests/backtest/`)\n- Replay historical data, verify decisions\n- MUST verify point-in-time integrity (filing_date filter applied)\n- Never use \"latest\" fundamental data in backtest path\n\n### LLM Extractor Snapshot Tests\n```python\n# tests/snapshots/test_claim_extraction.py\ndef test_claim_extraction_vcb_article() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Snapshot test — input text → expected structured output.\"\"\"\n    with open(\"tests/snapshots/vcb_q1_2026_article.txt\") as f:\n        article = f.read()\n    \n    result = extract_claims_from_article(article, use_cache=True)\n    \n    # Verify structure, not LLM creativity\n    assert all(c.source_url for c in result.claims)  # I-1\n    assert all(c.extracted_at for c in result.claims)  # I-2\n    assert all(0 <= c.confidence <= 1 for c in result.claims)\n    # Note: we test that numbers in claims came from source text, not LLM computation\n```\n\n### Calibration Tests\n```python\n# tests/calibration/test_kol_credibility.py\ndef test_credibility_score_converges_with_outcome_data() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Given 10 past recommendations with known outcomes, score should be ~0.7.\"\"\"\n    kol = make_kol()\n    outcomes = [True, True, False, True, True, False, True, True, True, False]\n    \n    for i, hit in enumerate(outcomes):\n        kol.record_recommendation_outcome(make_recommendation(i), hit)\n    \n    score = kol.credibility_score\n    assert 0.65 <= score.value <= 0.75, f\"Expected ~0.7, got {score.value}\"\n```\n\n## The 70-20-10 Guideline\n\nFor a mature codebase:\n- **70% unit tests**: Fast, numerous, cover domain logic\n- **20% integration tests**: Verify adapters work\n- **10% E2E/BDD tests**: Critical flows end-to-end\n\nIn MVP: closer to 50-40-10 may be acceptable. But don't let integration tests dominate — they're slow and brittle.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n### Testing LLM Output Content\n```python\n# Bad — asserting on LLM-generated text\ndef test_bear_case_mentions_risk():\n    result = llm_analyze_thesis(ticker=\"VCB\")\n    assert \"NPL\" in result.bear_case  # LLM might phrase it differently\n```\n\n### Correct\n```python\n# Good — test that bear case exists and is substantive (domain invariant)\ndef test_thesis_has_substantive_bear_case():\n    thesis = Thesis.create(ticker, bull, bear)\n    assert thesis.bear_case.is_substantive()  # domain method, not LLM assertion\n```\n\n### Testing LLM Math (should not exist)\n```python\n# This test should not exist — LLM should never compute numbers\ndef test_llm_computes_pe_ratio():\n    result = llm.analyze(ticker=\"VCB\")\n    assert result.pe_ratio == 12.5  # WRONG: LLM should not compute ratios\n```\n\n### Correct\n```python\n# Good — code computes, test verifies code\ndef test_pe_ratio_computation():\n    pe = compute_pe(price=Money.vnd(50_000), eps=Money.vnd(4_000))\n    assert pe == pytest.approx(12.5, rel=0.01)\n```\n\n## Detecting Imbalance\n\nRed flags:\n- Integration tests > unit tests in count (inverted pyramid)\n- Test suite > 5 min for unit layer (too many slow tests in unit)\n- E2E >20% of tests (expensive, brittle)\n- No BDD scenarios for top 3 user flows\n- Domain rules only verified through integration tests (slow, hard to debug)\n- Tests asserting on LLM-generated text content (fragile, wrong)\n\n## Coverage Targets\n\n### Domain layer (`packages/domain/`)\nTarget: 100% unit test coverage.\nNothing touches IO; no excuse for uncovered.\n\n### Application layer (`packages/application/`)\nTarget: 80% integration coverage.\nUse cases tested end-to-end with real DB.\n\n### Infrastructure (`packages/infrastructure/`)\nTarget: Adapter contract tests.\nEach adapter has integration test verifying it meets Protocol interface.\n\n## Related\n\n- `spec-dual-layer` — B.9 test requirements section\n- `ddd-tactical-patterns` — what's worth unit testing\n- `fastapi-module` — integration test setup (Phase 2+)\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"6ac8389d-ab78-402f-8273-ef7ed552cfc1","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

Verbatim pytest + gherkin templates.\n\n## Unit Test (Domain Logic)\n\n```python\n# packages/domain/analysis/tests/test_thesis.py\nimport pytest\nfrom packages.domain.analysis.models.thesis import Thesis, ThesisStatus\nfrom packages.domain.analysis.errors import InvariantViolation, InvalidStateError\n\ndef test_thesis_requires_substantive_bear_case() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Charter principle: adversarial by design — bear case mandatory.\"\"\"\n    with pytest.raises(InvariantViolation, match=\"bear case\"):\n        Thesis.create(\n            ticker=Ticker.from_str(\"VCB\"),\n            bull_case=BullCase(\"Strong earnings growth...\"),\n            bear_case=BearCase(\"\"),  # empty — must fail\n        )\n\ndef test_thesis_cannot_add_catalyst_when_active() -> None:\n    thesis = make_active_thesis()\n    with pytest.raises(InvalidStateError):\n        thesis.add_catalyst(make_catalyst())\n```\n\n## Integration Test (Use Case + Real DB)\n\n```python\n# apps/api/tests/test_validate_thesis_integration.py\nimport pytest\nfrom testcontainers.postgres import PostgresContainer\n\n@pytest.fixture(scope=\"session\")\ndef postgres():\n    with PostgresContainer(\"postgres:16\") as pg:\n        yield pg\n\nasync def test_validate_thesis_persists_and_emits_event(postgres, event_bus_mock):\n    repo = ThesisPostgresRepository(db=make_db(postgres))\n    use_case = ValidateThesisUseCase(thesis_repo=repo, event_bus=event_bus_mock)\n\n    result = await use_case.execute(\n        ticker=\"VCB\",\n        bull_case=\"Strong earnings growth driven by retail expansion...\",\n        bear_case=\"Rising NPL ratio may compress margins and trigger provision surge...\",\n    )\n\n    # Verify persistence\n    from_db = await repo.find_by_id(result.id)\n    assert from_db is not None\n    assert from_db.status == ThesisStatus.ACTIVE\n\n    # Verify event emitted\n    assert event_bus_mock.published_events[-1].type == \"ThesisCreated\"\n```\n\n## BDD Scenario\n\n```gherkin\n# bdd/features/validate_investment_thesis.feature\nFeature: Validate Investment Thesis\n\n  Scenario: User submits thesis with both bull and bear case\n    Given user is authenticated\n    When user submits thesis for ticker \"VCB\"\n      And bull case is \"Strong earnings growth...\"\n      And bear case is \"Rising NPL ratio may compress margins...\"\n    Then thesis status is \"active\"\n    And thesis has non-empty bear case\n    And ThesisCreated event is emitted\n```\n\n## LLM Extractor Snapshot Test\n\n```python\n# tests/snapshots/test_claim_extraction.py\ndef test_claim_extraction_vcb_article() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Snapshot test — input text → expected structured output.\n\n    We test that EVERY claim has the required structural fields.\n    We do NOT assert on specific LLM phrasing or numbers — that would\n    violate I-S1 (no LLM math) and produce a fragile test.\n    \"\"\"\n    with open(\"tests/snapshots/vcb_q1_2026_article.txt\") as f:\n        article = f.read()\n\n    result = extract_claims_from_article(article, use_cache=True)\n\n    assert all(c.source_url for c in result.claims)            # I-S1: source pointer\n    assert all(c.extracted_at for c in result.claims)          # I-S2: as-of date\n    assert all(0 <= c.confidence <= 1 for c in result.claims)  # bounded score\n    # Numbers in claims came from source text quotes, not LLM computation\n```\n\n## Calibration Test\n\n```python\n# tests/calibration/test_kol_credibility.py\ndef test_credibility_score_converges_with_outcome_data() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Given 10 past recommendations with known outcomes, score should be ~0.7.\"\"\"\n    kol = make_kol()\n    outcomes = [True, True, False, True, True, False, True, True, True, False]\n\n    for i, hit in enumerate(outcomes):\n        kol.record_recommendation_outcome(make_recommendation(i), hit)\n\n    score = kol.credibility_score\n    assert 0.65 <= score.value <= 0.75, f\"Expected ~0.7, got {score.value}\"\n```\n\n## Anti-Pattern Examples\n\n### Bad — asserting on LLM-generated text\n\n```python\ndef test_bear_case_mentions_risk():\n    result = llm_analyze_thesis(ticker=\"VCB\")\n    assert \"NPL\" in result.bear_case  # LLM might phrase it differently\n```\n\n### Good — test domain invariant\n\n```python\ndef test_thesis_has_substantive_bear_case():\n    thesis = Thesis.create(ticker, bull, bear)\n    assert thesis.bear_case.is_substantive()  # domain method, not LLM assertion\n```\n\n### Bad — testing LLM math (charter violation)\n\n```python\ndef test_llm_computes_pe_ratio():\n    result = llm.analyze(ticker=\"VCB\")\n    assert result.pe_ratio == 12.5  # WRONG: LLM should not compute ratios\n```\n\n### Good — code computes, test verifies code\n\n```python\ndef test_pe_ratio_computation():\n    pe = compute_pe(price=Money.vnd(50_000), eps=Money.vnd(4_000))\n    assert pe == pytest.approx(12.5, rel=0.01)\n```\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"3ad82d7a-da04-49aa-b592-7e4e21297f8d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"d1cc448d-090c-4358-ad88-b6c18f338b40","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":46,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"9a35461b-a672-4a73-a3b0-53d30d3f295a","timestamp":"2026-04-29T14:49:06.101Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"95d25c77-2cb2-416b-b074-0aefa3cdd9de","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"9500d654-bd35-4293-b673-30266423655a","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018VKmT7T1Nxfy6uL7iW2XVr","type":"tool_result","content":"---\nname: prompt-engineering\ndescription: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n---\n\n# Skill: Prompt Engineering\n\n## Purpose\n\nLLM prompts are data, not code. Treat them with same rigor as schemas.\n\n**Critical constraint**: LLM prompts in StockForge must NEVER ask LLM to compute numbers. LLM classifies, extracts, and reasons — deterministic code computes.\n\n## Where Prompts Live\n\n`prompts/` directory at project root:\n```\nprompts/\n├── extraction/\n│   ├── claim-from-article.md\n│   ├── kol-recommendation-from-transcript.md\n│   ├── sentiment-classification.md\n│   └── ...\n├── analysis/\n│   ├── bear-agent.md\n│   ├── bull-agent.md\n│   ├── critic-agent.md\n│   ├── pump-detection.md\n│   └── ...\n├── synthesis/\n│   └── thesis-synthesis.md\n└── _shared/\n    └── output-schemas.md\n```\n\nNOT embedded in Python code. DR4 catches this.\n\n## Prompt Structure (Template)\n\n```markdown\n---\nversion: 1.0\nowner: analysis-team\npurpose: Extract claims from single news article\ninput_schema: ArticleContent\noutput_schema: ClaimList\nmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6\nexpected_input_tokens: ~3000\nexpected_output_tokens: ~500\nno_llm_math: true  # REQUIRED: confirms this prompt does not ask LLM to compute numbers\n---\n\n# [System Prompt]\n\nYou are a claim extraction specialist for Vietnamese financial news. Your job is to\nidentify factual claims in the provided article and output them in structured format.\n\n## Rules\n1. Every claim must be supported by explicit text in the article\n2. Do not infer, interpret, or paraphrase heavily\n3. Use direct quotes when possible\n4. Assign confidence based on source clarity\n5. **NEVER compute financial ratios or percentages yourself** — extract numbers\n   verbatim from source text only. If a number is in the article, copy it.\n   Do not calculate.\n\n## Output Format\nReturn JSON matching this schema:\n{\n  \"claims\": [\n    {\n      \"text\": \"...\",\n      \"source_excerpt\": \"...\",\n      \"confidence\": 0.0-1.0,\n      \"type\": \"revenue_growth | profit | market_share | ...\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n\n# [User Message Template]\n\nArticle content:\n{{article_content}}\n\nExtract claims.\n```\n\n## No-LLM-Math Pattern\n\nThis is the most important constraint in StockForge prompts.\n\n### Wrong (LLM computes a number)\n```markdown\n# System\nGiven the financial data below, compute the P/E ratio and assess if it's attractive.\n```\n\n### Correct (LLM classifies, code computes)\n```python\n# Step 1: Code computes P/E\npe_ratio = compute_pe(price=stock.price, eps=fundamentals.eps)\n\n# Step 2: LLM only classifies the already-computed number\nprompt = f\"\"\"\nGiven P/E ratio of {pe_ratio:.1f} for {ticker} in the {sector} sector,\nclassify as: undervalued | fair_value | overvalued | cannot_assess\n\nHistorical sector P/E range: {sector_pe_5th:.1f} - {sector_pe_95th:.1f}\nCurrent market P/E: {market_pe:.1f}\n\nReturn classification only. Do not recompute the ratio.\n\"\"\"\n```\n\n## Prompt Caching Strategy\n\nAnthropic cache: 10× cost reduction + puts cached content at context head (highest attention).\n\n```python\n# What to cache (stable):\ncached_section = [\n    system_instructions,\n    output_schemas,\n    few_shot_examples,\n    domain_context,  # glossary excerpt for Vietnamese stock terms\n]\n\n# What NOT to cache (varies per call):\ndynamic_section = [\n    article_content,\n    current_timestamp,\n    ticker_specific_data,\n]\n\nresponse = await claude.messages.create(\n    model=\"claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n    system=[\n        {\n            \"type\": \"text\",\n            \"text\": section,\n            \"cache_control\": {\"type\": \"ephemeral\"},\n        }\n        for section in cached_section\n    ],\n    messages=[{\n        \"role\": \"user\",\n        \"content\": \"\\n\".join(dynamic_section),\n    }],\n)\n```\n\n## Budget-Aware Prompts\n\nEvery LLM call wrapped:\n\n```python\nfrom packages.infrastructure.llm.budget import with_budget\n\nresult = await with_budget(\n    max_cost_usd=0.50,\n    session_id=context.session_id,\n    purpose=\"claim-extraction\",\n)(claude.messages.create)(model=\"claude-sonnet-4-6\", ...)\n```\n\nIf cost would exceed cap, function throws before the call.\n\n## Structured Output Patterns\n\nUse Pydantic schemas (in infrastructure layer) for output validation:\n\n```python\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator\n\nclass ExtractedClaimDTO(BaseModel):\n    text: str\n    source_excerpt: str\n    confidence: float\n    claim_type: str\n\n    @field_validator(\"confidence\")\n    @classmethod\n    def validate_confidence(cls, v: float) -> float:\n        if not 0 <= v <= 1:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Confidence must be 0-1, got {v}\")\n        return v\n\nclass ClaimListDTO(BaseModel):\n    claims: list[ExtractedClaimDTO]\n\n# After LLM returns:\ntry:\n    parsed = ClaimListDTO.model_validate_json(response.content[0].text)\nexcept Exception as e:\n    # Retry with error feedback, or log and move on\n    logger.warning(\"LLM output parse failed\", error=str(e))\n```\n\n## Context Assembly for Thesis Synthesis\n\nFor complex analysis prompts, assemble context:\n\n1. **Core instruction** (stable, cached) — adversarial-by-default, no LLM math\n2. **Domain context** (glossary excerpt, Vietnam market context — cached if stable)\n3. **Pre-computed signals** (from deterministic code — NOT asked from LLM)\n4. **Task-specific data** (dynamic — thesis claims, KOL recs, sentiment scores)\n5. **Output schema** (cached)\n\n## Failure Modes\n\n**Output not valid JSON**:\n- Retry with stricter format reminder\n- Max 2 retries, then mark extraction failed\n\n**Output contradicts rules** (LLM computed a number):\n- Validate: does output contain a number that wasn't in the input?\n- Flag as I-S1 violation, do not use output\n\n**Budget exceeded mid-batch**:\n- Graceful degrade: return partial results\n- Mark batch as degraded, schedule continuation\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Hardcode long prompts in Python files (use prompts/*.md)\n- Skip output schema validation (get garbage responses)\n- Forget cache_control on stable sections (waste $)\n- Trust LLM output as ground truth (always verify)\n- Ask LLM to compute financial ratios, percentages, or prices (I-S1 violation)\n- Ask LLM for a single \"buy/sell/hold\" score (must be multi-criteria)\n\n**Do**:\n- Version prompts in git\n- A/B test prompt variants systematically\n- Cache stable content aggressively\n- Log tokens + cost per call for analysis\n- Pre-compute all numbers in Python, feed them as facts to LLM for classification only\n\n## Related\n\n- `evidence-extraction` — uses these prompts\n- `constitution/drift-signals.md` — DR3, DR4\n- `constitution/invariants.md` — I-S1 (No LLM {"parentUuid":"b51da4d1-8849-413d-8f8c-02310e3c56d0","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01UpwhLAoQ5sQKvGdWq15Kyi","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01VoAiYeugmPofWQvbuT8MP1","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\prompt-engineering\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: prompt-engineering\ndescription: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\nallowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Edit, Write]\n---\n\n# Skill: Prompt Engineering\n\n## Purpose\n\nLLM prompts are data, not code. Treat them with the same rigor as schemas — versioned, reviewed, A/B tested.\n\n**Critical constraint** (charter principle 9 / I-S1): LLM prompts in StockForge must NEVER ask the LLM to compute numbers. LLM classifies, extracts, and reasons. Deterministic code computes.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Authoring a new extractor (claim, KOL recommendation, sentiment)\n- Refining an existing prompt for cost / accuracy\n- Adding a new analysis agent (bear / bull / critic / quant / behavior)\n- Synthesizing a thesis with multi-source context\n- Investigating an output schema violation or hallucinated number\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Ad-hoc one-off chat queries (no production cost / governance)\n- Bash one-liners using LLM CLI for exploration\n\n## Where Prompts Live\n\n`prompts/` directory at project root, NOT inline in Python:\n\n```\nprompts/\n├── extraction/   (claim-from-article, kol-recommendation-from-transcript, sentiment-classification, ...)\n├── analysis/     (bear-agent, bull-agent, critic-agent, pump-detection, ...)\n├── synthesis/    (thesis-synthesis)\n└── _shared/      (output-schemas)\n```\n\nDR4 catches inline prompts. Always file-backed + version-controlled.\n\n## Mandatory Frontmatter\n\nEvery prompt file `prompts/**/*.md` MUST have:\n\n```yaml\n---\nversion: 1.0\nowner: <team>\npurpose: <one line>\ninput_schema: <DTO name>\noutput_schema: <DTO name>\nmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6  # or opus for synthesis\nexpected_input_tokens: ~N\nexpected_output_tokens: ~N\nno_llm_math: true  # REQUIRED: confirms prompt does not ask LLM to compute numbers\n---\n```\n\n`no_llm_math: true` is the BLOCKING field — drift hook scans for it; missing field = HIGH severity violation.\n\n## No-LLM-Math Pattern (the load-bearing rule)\n\n**Wrong** — LLM computes a number:\n\n> \"Given the financial data below, compute the P/E ratio and assess...\"\n\n**Correct** — code computes, LLM only classifies the already-computed number:\n\n```\nP/E ratio is 12.3 (computed by `compute_pe(price=..., eps=...)`).\nClassify as: undervalued | fair_value | overvalued | cannot_assess\nHistorical sector range: 8.5 - 18.2. Do not recompute.\n```\n\nThe number flows IN to the prompt as a fact; the LLM never produces a number that wasn't already in its input.\n\nSee `references/prompt-templates.md` for full system-prompt + classification-only examples.\n\n## Caching Strategy\n\nAnthropic prompt cache: 10× cost reduction + puts cached content at context head (highest attention).\n\n| Cache | Don't cache |\n|---|---|\n| System instructions | Article content, transcript |\n| Output schemas | Current timestamp |\n| Few-shot examples | Ticker-specific data |\n| Domain context (Vietnamese stock glossary excerpt) | Pre-computed signals (these change per call) |\n\nUse `cache_control: {\"type\": \"ephemeral\"}` on stable sections. See `references/prompt-templates.md` § Caching.\n\n## Budget Wrapper\n\nEvery LLM call goes through the budget wrapper:\n\n```python\nfrom packages.infrastructure.llm.budget import with_budget\n\nresult = await with_budget(max_cost_usd=0.50, session_id=ctx.session_id, purpose=\"claim-extraction\")(\n    claude.messages.create\n)(model=\"claude-sonnet-4-6\", ...)\n```\n\nIf projected cost > cap, the wrapper throws BEFORE the call.\n\n## Structured Output\n\nValidate with Pydantic DTOs **at the infrastructure boundary** (NOT in the domain layer):\n\n```python\nclass ExtractedClaimDTO(BaseModel):\n    text: str\n    source_excerpt: str\n    confidence: float  # validated 0-1 via field_validator\n    claim_type: str\n\nparsed = ExtractedClaimDTO.model_validate_json(response.content[0].text)\n```\n\nRetry on parse error (max 2). After retries, log + degrade.\n\n## Failure Modes\n\n| Symptom | Action |\n|---|---|\n| Output not valid JSON | Retry with stricter format reminder; max 2; then mark extraction failed |\n| LLM produced a number not in input | Flag as I-S1 violation; reject output |\n| Budget exceeded mid-batch | Graceful degrade; return partial; schedule continuation |\n| Output asserts confidence > 1.0 | Field validator rejects; clamp to [0,1] is forbidden |\n\n## Validation Pre-Conditions\n\n- File lives under `prompts/**/*.md` (not embedded in `.py`) — DR4 enforces\n- Frontmatter has `no_llm_math: true`\n- Prompt does NOT contain words like \"compute\", \"calculate\", \"what is X%\" near a number request\n- Output schema is in `prompts/_shared/output-schemas.md` AND has matching DTO in `packages/infrastructure/llm/dtos/`\n- Caching policy: stable sections marked with `cache_control`\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Hardcode long prompts in Python files (use `prompts/*.md` + DR4 hook)\n- Skip output schema validation (garbage in production)\n- Forget `cache_control` on stable sections (10× wasted cost)\n- Trust LLM output as ground truth (always verify against source quotes)\n- Ask LLM to compute ratios, percentages, prices, or rank scores (I-S1)\n- Ask LLM for a single \"buy/sell/hold\" score (must be multi-criteria — charter principle 2)\n\n**Do**:\n- Version prompts in git\n- A/B test variants systematically against eval set\n- Cache stable content aggressively\n- Log tokens + cost per call into `agent-workspace/calibration/`\n- Pre-compute every number in Python; feed as fact to LLM for classification only\n- Pass scoring rubrics as cached system context, not per-call\n\n## Smoke Test\n\nFor task \"extract claims from a CafeF article\":\n\nExpected prompt shape:\n- File at `prompts/extraction/claim-from-article.md`\n- Frontmatter: `no_llm_math: true`, `model: claude-sonnet-4-6`, `output_schema: ClaimListDTO`\n- System prompt contains: \"Use direct quotes\", \"NEVER compute ratios — extract numbers verbatim\"\n- Output schema cached; `{{article_content}}` placeholder for dynamic input\n- Python wrapper uses `with_budget(...)` + Pydantic validation\n\nIf the proposed prompt asks the LLM to \"calculate\" or \"estimate\" a number → reject.\n\n## See Also\n\n- `references/prompt-templates.md` — full prompt frontmatter + caching code + Pydantic DTO + context assembly checklist\n- `evidence-extraction` SKILL.md — consumes these prompts\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` — DR3 + DR4 (inline-prompt + no-llm-math hooks)\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/invariants.md` — I-S1 (No LLM Math) authoritative spec\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2973,"cache_read_input_tokens":228157,"output_tokens":5081,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2973,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":5081,"cache_read_input_tokens":228157,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2973,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2973},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYFPQ1UssQ8X3i7jQ4bq","type":"assistant","uuid":"60230222-8d42-4dc1-b007-658a3095d6ea","timestamp":"2026-04-29T14:50:13.548Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

authoritative spec"]}],"originalFile":"---\nname: prompt-engineering\ndescription: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n---\n\n# Skill: Prompt Engineering\n\n## Purpose\n\nLLM prompts are data, not code. Treat them with same rigor as schemas.\n\n**Critical constraint**: LLM prompts in StockForge must NEVER ask LLM to compute numbers. LLM classifies, extracts, and reasons — deterministic code computes.\n\n## Where Prompts Live\n\n`prompts/` directory at project root:\n```\nprompts/\n├── extraction/\n│   ├── claim-from-article.md\n│   ├── kol-recommendation-from-transcript.md\n│   ├── sentiment-classification.md\n│   └── ...\n├── analysis/\n│   ├── bear-agent.md\n│   ├── bull-agent.md\n│   ├── critic-agent.md\n│   ├── pump-detection.md\n│   └── ...\n├── synthesis/\n│   └── thesis-synthesis.md\n└── _shared/\n    └── output-schemas.md\n```\n\nNOT embedded in Python code. DR4 catches this.\n\n## Prompt Structure (Template)\n\n```markdown\n---\nversion: 1.0\nowner: analysis-team\npurpose: Extract claims from single news article\ninput_schema: ArticleContent\noutput_schema: ClaimList\nmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6\nexpected_input_tokens: ~3000\nexpected_output_tokens: ~500\nno_llm_math: true  # REQUIRED: confirms this prompt does not ask LLM to compute numbers\n---\n\n# [System Prompt]\n\nYou are a claim extraction specialist for Vietnamese financial news. Your job is to\nidentify factual claims in the provided article and output them in structured format.\n\n## Rules\n1. Every claim must be supported by explicit text in the article\n2. Do not infer, interpret, or paraphrase heavily\n3. Use direct quotes when possible\n4. Assign confidence based on source clarity\n5. **NEVER compute financial ratios or percentages yourself** — extract numbers\n   verbatim from source text only. If a number is in the article, copy it.\n   Do not calculate.\n\n## Output Format\nReturn JSON matching this schema:\n{\n  \"claims\": [\n    {\n      \"text\": \"...\",\n      \"source_excerpt\": \"...\",\n      \"confidence\": 0.0-1.0,\n      \"type\": \"revenue_growth | profit | market_share | ...\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n\n# [User Message Template]\n\nArticle content:\n{{article_content}}\n\nExtract claims.\n```\n\n## No-LLM-Math Pattern\n\nThis is the most important constraint in StockForge prompts.\n\n### Wrong (LLM computes a number)\n```markdown\n# System\nGiven the financial data below, compute the P/E ratio and assess if it's attractive.\n```\n\n### Correct (LLM classifies, code computes)\n```python\n# Step 1: Code computes P/E\npe_ratio = compute_pe(price=stock.price, eps=fundamentals.eps)\n\n# Step 2: LLM only classifies the already-computed number\nprompt = f\"\"\"\nGiven P/E ratio of {pe_ratio:.1f} for {ticker} in the {sector} sector,\nclassify as: undervalued | fair_value | overvalued | cannot_assess\n\nHistorical sector P/E range: {sector_pe_5th:.1f} - {sector_pe_95th:.1f}\nCurrent market P/E: {market_pe:.1f}\n\nReturn classification only. Do not recompute the ratio.\n\"\"\"\n```\n\n## Prompt Caching Strategy\n\nAnthropic cache: 10× cost reduction + puts cached content at context head (highest attention).\n\n```python\n# What to cache (stable):\ncached_section = [\n    system_instructions,\n    output_schemas,\n    few_shot_examples,\n    domain_context,  # glossary excerpt for Vietnamese stock terms\n]\n\n# What NOT to cache (varies per call):\ndynamic_section = [\n    article_content,\n    current_timestamp,\n    ticker_specific_data,\n]\n\nresponse = await claude.messages.create(\n    model=\"claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n    system=[\n        {\n            \"type\": \"text\",\n            \"text\": section,\n            \"cache_control\": {\"type\": \"ephemeral\"},\n        }\n        for section in cached_section\n    ],\n    messages=[{\n        \"role\": \"user\",\n        \"content\": \"\\n\".join(dynamic_section),\n    }],\n)\n```\n\n## Budget-Aware Prompts\n\nEvery LLM call wrapped:\n\n```python\nfrom packages.infrastructure.llm.budget import with_budget\n\nresult = await with_budget(\n    max_cost_usd=0.50,\n    session_id=context.session_id,\n    purpose=\"claim-extraction\",\n)(claude.messages.create)(model=\"claude-sonnet-4-6\", ...)\n```\n\nIf cost would exceed cap, function throws before the call.\n\n## Structured Output Patterns\n\nUse Pydantic schemas (in infrastructure layer) for output validation:\n\n```python\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator\n\nclass ExtractedClaimDTO(BaseModel):\n    text: str\n    source_excerpt: str\n    confidence: float\n    claim_type: str\n\n    @field_validator(\"confidence\")\n    @classmethod\n    def validate_confidence(cls, v: float) -> float:\n        if not 0 <= v <= 1:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Confidence must be 0-1, got {v}\")\n        return v\n\nclass ClaimListDTO(BaseModel):\n    claims: list[ExtractedClaimDTO]\n\n# After LLM returns:\ntry:\n    parsed = ClaimListDTO.model_validate_json(response.content[0].text)\nexcept Exception as e:\n    # Retry with error feedback, or log and move on\n    logger.warning(\"LLM output parse failed\", error=str(e))\n```\n\n## Context Assembly for Thesis Synthesis\n\nFor complex analysis prompts, assemble context:\n\n1. **Core instruction** (stable, cached) — adversarial-by-default, no LLM math\n2. **Domain context** (glossary excerpt, Vietnam market context — cached if stable)\n3. **Pre-computed signals** (from deterministic code — NOT asked from LLM)\n4. **Task-specific data** (dynamic — thesis claims, KOL recs, sentiment scores)\n5. **Output schema** (cached)\n\n## Failure Modes\n\n**Output not valid JSON**:\n- Retry with stricter format reminder\n- Max 2 retries, then mark extraction failed\n\n**Output contradicts rules** (LLM computed a number):\n- Validate: does output contain a number that wasn't in the input?\n- Flag as I-S1 violation, do not use output\n\n**Budget exceeded mid-batch**:\n- Graceful degrade: return partial results\n- Mark batch as degraded, schedule continuation\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Hardcode long prompts in Python files (use prompts/*.md)\n- Skip output schema validation (get garbage responses)\n- Forget cache_control on stable sections (waste $)\n- Trust LLM output as ground truth (always verify)\n- Ask LLM to compute financial ratios, percentages, or prices (I-S1 violation)\n- Ask LLM for a single \"buy/sell/hold\" score (must be multi-criteria)\n\n**Do**:\n- Version prompts in git\n- A/B test prompt variants systematically\n- Cache stable content aggressively\n- Log tokens + cost per call for analysis\n- Pre-compute all numbers in Python, feed them as facts to LLM for classification only\n\n## Related\n\n- `evidence-extraction` — uses these prompts\n- `constitution/drift-signals.md` — DR3, DR4\n- `constitution/invariants.md` — I-S1 (No LLM Math)\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"60230222-8d42-4dc1-b007-658a3095d6ea","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

Verbatim templates and code blocks.\n\n## Full Prompt File Template\n\n```markdown\n---\nversion: 1.0\nowner: analysis-team\npurpose: Extract claims from single news article\ninput_schema: ArticleContent\noutput_schema: ClaimList\nmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6\nexpected_input_tokens: ~3000\nexpected_output_tokens: ~500\nno_llm_math: true  # REQUIRED\n---\n\n# [System Prompt]\n\nYou are a claim extraction specialist for Vietnamese financial news. Your job is\nto identify factual claims in the provided article and output them in structured\nformat.\n\n## Rules\n1. Every claim must be supported by explicit text in the article\n2. Do not infer, interpret, or paraphrase heavily\n3. Use direct quotes when possible\n4. Assign confidence based on source clarity\n5. **NEVER compute financial ratios or percentages yourself** — extract numbers\n   verbatim from source text only. If a number is in the article, copy it.\n   Do not calculate.\n\n## Output Format\nReturn JSON matching this schema:\n{\n  \"claims\": [\n    {\n      \"text\": \"...\",\n      \"source_excerpt\": \"...\",\n      \"confidence\": 0.0-1.0,\n      \"type\": \"revenue_growth | profit | market_share | ...\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n\n# [User Message Template]\n\nArticle content:\n{{article_content}}\n\nExtract claims.\n```\n\n## No-LLM-Math — Wrong vs Correct\n\n**Wrong**:\n\n```markdown\n# System\nGiven the financial data below, compute the P/E ratio and assess if it's attractive.\n```\n\n**Correct** (code computes, LLM classifies):\n\n```python\n# Step 1: Code computes P/E\npe_ratio = compute_pe(price=stock.price, eps=fundamentals.eps)\n\n# Step 2: LLM only classifies the already-computed number\nprompt = f\"\"\"\nGiven P/E ratio of {pe_ratio:.1f} for {ticker} in the {sector} sector,\nclassify as: undervalued | fair_value | overvalued | cannot_assess\n\nHistorical sector P/E range: {sector_pe_5th:.1f} - {sector_pe_95th:.1f}\nCurrent market P/E: {market_pe:.1f}\n\nReturn classification only. Do not recompute the ratio.\n\"\"\"\n```\n\n## Caching — Stable vs Dynamic Split\n\n```python\n# What to cache (stable):\ncached_section = [\n    system_instructions,\n    output_schemas,\n    few_shot_examples,\n    domain_context,  # Vietnamese stock glossary excerpt\n]\n\n# What NOT to cache (varies per call):\ndynamic_section = [\n    article_content,\n    current_timestamp,\n    ticker_specific_data,\n]\n\nresponse = await claude.messages.create(\n    model=\"claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n    system=[\n        {\n            \"type\": \"text\",\n            \"text\": section,\n            \"cache_control\": {\"type\": \"ephemeral\"},\n        }\n        for section in cached_section\n    ],\n    messages=[{\n        \"role\": \"user\",\n        \"content\": \"\\n\".join(dynamic_section),\n    }],\n)\n```\n\n## Budget Wrapper\n\n```python\nfrom packages.infrastructure.llm.budget import with_budget\n\nresult = await with_budget(\n    max_cost_usd=0.50,\n    session_id=context.session_id,\n    purpose=\"claim-extraction\",\n)(claude.messages.create)(model=\"claude-sonnet-4-6\", ...)\n```\n\nIf projected cost would exceed cap, function throws BEFORE the call.\n\n## Structured Output — Pydantic DTO\n\n```python\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator\n\nclass ExtractedClaimDTO(BaseModel):\n    text: str\n    source_excerpt: str\n    confidence: float\n    claim_type: str\n\n    @field_validator(\"confidence\")\n    @classmethod\n    def validate_confidence(cls, v: float) -> float:\n        if not 0 <= v <= 1:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Confidence must be 0-1, got {v}\")\n        return v\n\nclass ClaimListDTO(BaseModel):\n    claims: list[ExtractedClaimDTO]\n\n# After LLM returns:\ntry:\n    parsed = ClaimListDTO.model_validate_json(response.content[0].text)\nexcept Exception as e:\n    # Retry with error feedback, or log and move on\n    logger.warning(\"LLM output parse failed\", error=str(e))\n```\n\n## Context Assembly Checklist (Thesis Synthesis)\n\nFor complex analysis prompts, assemble in this order:\n\n1. **Core instruction** (stable, cached) — adversarial-by-default, no LLM math\n2. **Domain context** (glossary excerpt, Vietnam market context — cached if stable)\n3. **Pre-computed signals** (from deterministic code — NOT asked from LLM)\n4. **Task-specific data** (dynamic — thesis claims, KOL recs, sentiment scores)\n5. **Output schema** (cached)\n\nThe LLM sees: stable cached content first → dynamic input → must produce structured output. Verbatim templates and code blocks.\n\n## Full Prompt File Template\n\n```markdown\n---\nversion: 1.0\nowner: analysis-team\npurpose: Extract claims from single news article\ninput_schema: ArticleContent\noutput_schema: ClaimList\nmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6\nexpected_input_tokens: ~3000\nexpected_output_tokens: ~500\nno_llm_math: true  # REQUIRED\n---\n\n# [System Prompt]\n\nYou are a claim extraction specialist for Vietnamese financial news. Your job is\nto identify factual claims in the provided article and output them in structured\nformat.\n\n## Rules\n1. Every claim must be supported by explicit text in the article\n2. Do not infer, interpret, or paraphrase heavily\n3. Use direct quotes when possible\n4. Assign confidence based on source clarity\n5. **NEVER compute financial ratios or percentages yourself** — extract numbers\n   verbatim from source text only. If a number is in the article, copy it.\n   Do not calculate.\n\n## Output Format\nReturn JSON matching this schema:\n{\n  \"claims\": [\n    {\n      \"text\": \"...\",\n      \"source_excerpt\": \"...\",\n      \"confidence\": 0.0-1.0,\n      \"type\": \"revenue_growth | profit | market_share | ...\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n\n# [User Message Template]\n\nArticle content:\n{{article_content}}\n\nExtract claims.\n```\n\n## No-LLM-Math — Wrong vs Correct\n\n**Wrong**:\n\n```markdown\n# System\nGiven the financial data below, compute the P/E ratio and assess if it's attractive.\n```\n\n**Correct** (code computes, LLM classifies):\n\n```python\n# Step 1: Code computes P/E\npe_ratio = compute_pe(price=stock.price, eps=fundamentals.eps)\n\n# Step 2: LLM only classifies the already-computed number\nprompt = f\"\"\"\nGiven P/E ratio of {pe_ratio:.1f} for {ticker} in the {sector} sector,\nclassify as: undervalued | fair_value | overvalued | cannot_assess\n\nHistorical sector P/E range: {sector_pe_5th:.1f} - {sector_pe_95th:.1f}\nCurrent market P/E: {market_pe:.1f}\n\nReturn classification only. Do not recompute the ratio.\n\"\"\"\n```\n\n## Caching — Stable vs Dynamic Split\n\n```python\n# What to cache (stable):\ncached_section = [\n    system_instructions,\n    output_schemas,\n    few_shot_examples,\n    domain_context,  # Vietnamese stock glossary excerpt\n]\n\n# What NOT to cache (varies per call):\ndynamic_section = [\n    article_content,\n    current_timestamp,\n    ticker_specific_data,\n]\n\nresponse = await claude.messages.create(\n    model=\"claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n    system=[\n        {\n            \"type\": \"text\",\n            \"text\": section,\n            \"cache_control\": {\"type\": \"ephemeral\"},\n        }\n        for section in cached_section\n    ],\n    messages=[{\n        \"role\": \"user\",\n        \"content\": \"\\n\".join(dynamic_section),\n    }],\n)\n```\n\n## Budget Wrapper\n\n```python\nfrom packages.infrastructure.llm.budget import with_budget\n\nresult = await with_budget(\n    max_cost_usd=0.50,\n    session_id=context.session_id,\n    purpose=\"claim-extraction\",\n)(claude.messages.create)(model=\"claude-sonnet-4-6\", ...)\n```\n\nIf projected cost would exceed cap, function throws BEFORE the call.\n\n## Structured Output — Pydantic DTO\n\n```python\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator\n\nclass ExtractedClaimDTO(BaseModel):\n    text: str\n    source_excerpt: str\n    confidence: float\n    claim_type: str\n\n    @field_validator(\"confidence\")\n    @classmethod\n    def validate_confidence(cls, v: float) -> float:\n        if not 0 <= v <= 1:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Confidence must be 0-1, got {v}\")\n        return v\n\nclass ClaimListDTO(BaseModel):\n    claims: list[ExtractedClaimDTO]\n\n# After LLM returns:\ntry:\n    parsed = ClaimListDTO.model_validate_json(response.content[0].text)\nexcept Exception as e:\n    # Retry with error feedback, or log and move on\n    logger.warning(\"LLM output parse failed\", error=str(e))\n```\n\n## Context Assembly Checklist (Thesis Synthesis)\n\nFor complex analysis prompts, assemble in this order:\n\n1. **Core instruction** (stable, cached) — adversarial-by-default, no LLM math\n2. **Domain context** (glossary excerpt, Vietnam market context — cached if stable)\n3. **Pre-computed signals** (from deterministic code — NOT asked from LLM)\n4. **Task-specific data** (dynamic — thesis claims, KOL recs, sentiment scores)\n5. **Output schema** (cached)\n\nThe LLM sees: stable cached content first → dynamic input → must produce structured output. This ordering matches Anthropic's attention-first cache placement.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"49ea33e0-5e17-416e-aff5-ae069eaea1ff","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\".
