{"parentUuid":"32acdccd-a372-45a5-ab5b-5d47ac8c908d","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01Vc5gmgoc9nPrxcxGP8hgTG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01FJdYNkRR4ywxuTNSFbpc3B","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\prompt-engineering\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: prompt-engineering\ndescription: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\nallowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Edit, Write]\n---\n\n# Skill: Prompt Engineering\n\n## Purpose\n\nLLM prompts are data, not code. Treat them with the same rigor as schemas — versioned, reviewed, A/B tested.\n\n**Critical constraint** (charter principle 9 / I-S1): LLM prompts NEVER ask the LLM to compute numbers. LLM classifies, extracts, reasons. Deterministic code computes.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Authoring a new extractor (claim, KOL recommendation, sentiment)\n- Refining an existing prompt for cost / accuracy\n- Adding a new analysis agent (bear / bull / critic / quant / behavior)\n- Synthesizing a thesis with multi-source context\n- Investigating an output schema violation or hallucinated number\n\n## Where Prompts Live\n\n`prompts/` directory — NOT inline in Python (DR4 hook flags violations):\n\n```\nprompts/{extraction,analysis,synthesis,_shared}/\n```\n\n## Mandatory Frontmatter\n\nEvery `prompts/**/*.md` MUST include:\n\n```yaml\n---\nversion: 1.0\nowner: <team>\npurpose: <one line>\ninput_schema: <DTO>\noutput_schema: <DTO>\nmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6   # or opus for synthesis\nexpected_input_tokens: ~N\nexpected_output_tokens: ~N\nno_llm_math: true          # BLOCKING — drift hook scans for it\n---\n```\n\nMissing `no_llm_math: true` = HIGH severity drift violation.\n\n## No-LLM-Math Pattern (load-bearing)\n\n**Wrong** — LLM computes a number:\n> \"Given the financial data below, compute the P/E ratio and assess...\"\n\n**Correct** — code computes, LLM only classifies the already-computed number:\n\n```\nP/E ratio is 12.3 (computed by `compute_pe(price, eps)`).\nClassify as: undervalued | fair_value | overvalued | cannot_assess\nHistorical sector range: 8.5 - 18.2. Do not recompute.\n```\n\nNumbers flow IN as facts; the LLM never produces a number absent from its input. See `references/prompt-templates.md` § No-LLM-Math for full wrong/correct code blocks.\n\n## Caching\n\nAnthropic prompt cache — 10× cost reduction + cached content sits at context head (highest attention).\n\n| Cache (stable) | Don't cache (per-call) |\n|---|---|\n| System instructions | Article content / transcript |\n| Output schemas | Current timestamp |\n| Few-shot examples | Ticker-specific data |\n| Domain glossary excerpt | Pre-computed signals |\n\nMark with `cache_control: {\"type\": \"ephemeral\"}`. See `references/prompt-templates.md` § Caching.\n\n## Budget + Validation\n\n- Every LLM call wraps via `with_budget(max_cost_usd=..., session_id=..., purpose=...)` (throws BEFORE call if cost projection exceeds cap)\n- Every LLM output validates via Pydantic DTO at infrastructure boundary (NOT in domain). Retry on parse error, max 2; then degrade.\n\nCode in `references/prompt-templates.md` § Budget + § Pydantic.\n\n## Failure Modes\n\n| Symptom | Action |\n|---|---|\n| Output not valid JSON | Retry with stricter format reminder; max 2; mark failed |\n| LLM produced number not in input | Flag I-S1 violation; reject output |\n| Budget exceeded mid-batch | Graceful degrade; return partial; schedule continuation |\n| Output `confidence > 1.0` | Field validator rejects; do NOT clamp silently |\n\n## Validation Pre-Conditions\n\n- File lives under `prompts/**/*.md` (DR4 enforces)\n- Frontmatter has `no_llm_math: true`\n- Prompt does NOT contain \"compute\" / \"calculate\" / \"what is X%\" near a number request\n- Output schema has matching DTO under `packages/infrastructure/llm/dtos/`\n- Stable sections marked `cache_control`\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Hardcode prompts in `.py` (DR4 catches)\n- Skip output schema validation\n- Forget `cache_control` on stable sections (10× wasted cost)\n- Trust LLM output as ground truth without source-quote check\n- Ask LLM for ratios, percentages, prices, ranks (I-S1)\n- Ask LLM for a single \"buy/sell/hold\" score (must be multi-criteria — charter principle 2)\n\n**Do**:\n- Version prompts in git\n- A/B test variants against an eval set\n- Cache stable content aggressively\n- Log tokens + cost per call to `agent-workspace/calibration/`\n- Pre-compute every number in Python; feed as fact for classification only\n\n## Smoke Test\n\nFor \"extract claims from a CafeF article\":\n\nExpected:\n- File at `prompts/extraction/claim-from-article.md`\n- Frontmatter has `no_llm_math: true`, `output_schema: ClaimListDTO`\n- System prompt: \"Use direct quotes\", \"NEVER compute ratios — extract numbers verbatim\"\n- `{{article_content}}` placeholder; output schema cached\n- Python wrapper uses `with_budget(...)` + `ClaimListDTO.model_validate_json(...)`\n\nIf proposal asks LLM to \"calculate\" or \"estimate\" a number → reject.\n\n## See Also\n\n- `references/prompt-templates.md` — full frontmatter + no-llm-math + caching + budget + Pydantic + context-assembly checklist\n- `evidence-extraction` SKILL.md — consumes these prompts\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` — DR3 / DR4\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/invariants.md` — I-S1 authoritative spec\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":9518,"cache_read_input_tokens":231130,"output_tokens":2752,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":9518,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":2752,"cache_read_input_tokens":231130,"cache_creation_input_tokens":9518,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":9518},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYFTnCqQ5U7szeAyyUP5","type":"assistant","uuid":"5a9fc66e-2044-4488-b384-9d0ae3295977","timestamp":"2026-04-29T14:51:12.863Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\nallowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Edit, Write]\n---\n\n# Skill: Prompt Engineering\n\n## Purpose\n\nLLM prompts are data, not code. Treat them with the same rigor as schemas — versioned, reviewed, A/B tested.\n\n**Critical constraint** (charter principle 9 / I-S1): LLM prompts in StockForge must NEVER ask the LLM to compute numbers. LLM classifies, extracts, and reasons. Deterministic code computes.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Authoring a new extractor (claim, KOL recommendation, sentiment)\n- Refining an existing prompt for cost / accuracy\n- Adding a new analysis agent (bear / bull / critic / quant / behavior)\n- Synthesizing a thesis with multi-source context\n- Investigating an output schema violation or hallucinated number\n\n## When NOT to Use\n\n- Ad-hoc one-off chat queries (no production cost / governance)\n- Bash one-liners using LLM CLI for exploration\n\n## Where Prompts Live\n\n`prompts/` directory at project root, NOT inline in Python:\n\n```\nprompts/\n├── extraction/   (claim-from-article, kol-recommendation-from-transcript, sentiment-classification, ...)\n├── analysis/     (bear-agent, bull-agent, critic-agent, pump-detection, ...)\n├── synthesis/    (thesis-synthesis)\n└── _shared/      (output-schemas)\n```\n\nDR4 catches inline prompts. Always file-backed + version-controlled.\n\n## Mandatory Frontmatter\n\nEvery prompt file `prompts/**/*.md` MUST have:\n\n```yaml\n---\nversion: 1.0\nowner: <team>\npurpose: <one line>\ninput_schema: <DTO name>\noutput_schema: <DTO name>\nmodel: claude-sonnet-4-6  # or opus for synthesis\nexpected_input_tokens: ~N\nexpected_output_tokens: ~N\nno_llm_math: true  # REQUIRED: confirms prompt does not ask LLM to compute numbers\n---\n```\n\n`no_llm_math: true` is the BLOCKING field — drift hook scans for it; missing field = HIGH severity violation.\n\n## No-LLM-Math Pattern (the load-bearing rule)\n\n**Wrong** — LLM computes a number:\n\n> \"Given the financial data below, compute the P/E ratio and assess...\"\n\n**Correct** — code computes, LLM only classifies the already-computed number:\n\n```\nP/E ratio is 12.3 (computed by `compute_pe(price=..., eps=...)`).\nClassify as: undervalued | fair_value | overvalued | cannot_assess\nHistorical sector range: 8.5 - 18.2. Do not recompute.\n```\n\nThe number flows IN to the prompt as a fact; the LLM never produces a number that wasn't already in its input.\n\nSee `references/prompt-templates.md` for full system-prompt + classification-only examples.\n\n## Caching Strategy\n\nAnthropic prompt cache: 10× cost reduction + puts cached content at context head (highest attention).\n\n| Cache | Don't cache |\n|---|---|\n| System instructions | Article content, transcript |\n| Output schemas | Current timestamp |\n| Few-shot examples | Ticker-specific data |\n| Domain context (Vietnamese stock glossary excerpt) | Pre-computed signals (these change per call) |\n\nUse `cache_control: {\"type\": \"ephemeral\"}` on stable sections. See `references/prompt-templates.md` § Caching.\n\n## Budget Wrapper\n\nEvery LLM call goes through the budget wrapper:\n\n```python\nfrom packages.infrastructure.llm.budget import with_budget\n\nresult = await with_budget(max_cost_usd=0.50, session_id=ctx.session_id, purpose=\"claim-extraction\")(\n    claude.messages.create\n)(model=\"claude-sonnet-4-6\", ...)\n```\n\nIf projected cost > cap, the wrapper throws BEFORE the call.\n\n## Structured Output\n\nValidate with Pydantic DTOs **at the infrastructure boundary** (NOT in the domain layer):\n\n```python\nclass ExtractedClaimDTO(BaseModel):\n    text: str\n    source_excerpt: str\n    confidence: float  # validated 0-1 via field_validator\n    claim_type: str\n\nparsed = ExtractedClaimDTO.model_validate_json(response.content[0].text)\n```\n\nRetry on parse error (max 2). After retries, log + degrade.\n\n## Failure Modes\n\n| Symptom | Action |\n|---|---|\n| Output not valid JSON | Retry with stricter format reminder; max 2; then mark extraction failed |\n| LLM produced a number not in input | Flag as I-S1 violation; reject output |\n| Budget exceeded mid-batch | Graceful degrade; return partial; schedule continuation |\n| Output asserts confidence > 1.0 | Field validator rejects; clamp to [0,1] is forbidden |\n\n## Validation Pre-Conditions\n\n- File lives under `prompts/**/*.md` (not embedded in `.py`) — DR4 enforces\n- Frontmatter has `no_llm_math: true`\n- Prompt does NOT contain words like \"compute\", \"calculate\", \"what is X%\" near a number request\n- Output schema is in `prompts/_shared/output-schemas.md` AND has matching DTO in `packages/infrastructure/llm/dtos/`\n- Caching policy: stable sections marked with `cache_control`\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n**Don't**:\n- Hardcode long prompts in Python files (use `prompts/*.md` + DR4 hook)\n- Skip output schema validation (garbage in production)\n- Forget `cache_control` on stable sections (10× wasted cost)\n- Trust LLM output as ground truth (always verify against source quotes)\n- Ask LLM to compute ratios, percentages, prices, or rank scores (I-S1)\n- Ask LLM for a single \"buy/sell/hold\" score (must be multi-criteria — charter principle 2)\n\n**Do**:\n- Version prompts in git\n- A/B test variants systematically against eval set\n- Cache stable content aggressively\n- Log tokens + cost per call into `agent-workspace/calibration/`\n- Pre-compute every number in Python; feed as fact to LLM for classification only\n- Pass scoring rubrics as cached system context, not per-call\n\n## Smoke Test\n\nFor task \"extract claims from a CafeF article\":\n\nExpected prompt shape:\n- File at `prompts/extraction/claim-from-article.md`\n- Frontmatter: `no_llm_math: true`, `model: claude-sonnet-4-6`, `output_schema: ClaimListDTO`\n- System prompt contains: \"Use direct quotes\", \"NEVER compute ratios — extract numbers verbatim\"\n- Output schema cached; `{{article_content}}` placeholder for dynamic input\n- Python wrapper uses `with_budget(...)` + Pydantic validation\n\nIf the proposed prompt asks the LLM to \"calculate\" or \"estimate\" a number → reject.\n\n## See Also\n\n- `references/prompt-templates.md` — full prompt frontmatter + caching code + Pydantic DTO + context assembly checklist\n- `evidence-extraction` SKILL.md — consumes these prompts\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/drift-signals.md` — DR3 + DR4 (inline-prompt + no-llm-math hooks)\n- `agent-workspace/constitution/invariants.md` — I-S1 (No LLM Math) authoritative spec\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"5a9fc66e-2044-4488-b384-9d0ae3295977","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"479ff6ec-93b1-483f-b31b-4ba2ea355a16","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. {"parentUuid":"41f1d163-cd0b-4495-b109-c97454900a08","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"9500d654-bd35-4293-b673-30266423655a","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XY72Per1hb2Rp8jLK9xxkF","type":"tool_result","content":"---\nname: spec-dual-layer\ndescription: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n---\n\n# Skill: Dual-Layer Spec Authoring\n\n## Purpose\n\nEvery feature spec serves two audiences with different needs:\n- **Human stakeholder**: narrative, context, rationale\n- **AI agent**: structure, unambiguous contracts, machine-verifiable\n\nThis skill teaches the dual-layer pattern for specs that serve both.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Writing any Tier 2 (feature) spec\n- Writing any Tier 3 (task) spec\n- Refactoring existing spec to dual-layer format\n- Reviewing a spec for completeness\n\n## The Template\n\nReference: `/SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` at project root.\n\nThree parts:\n- **Part A**: Business Specification (narrative)\n- **Part B**: Agent Contract (structured)\n- **Part C**: Provenance & Review (living log)\n\n## Part A Guidelines\n\n### Goal\nMake it readable by non-engineer stakeholders. Business Analyst mindset.\n\n### What belongs in Part A\n\n- **A.1 Context**: Why this exists, what problem it solves, narrative\n- **A.2 User & Use Cases**: Who uses this, concrete scenarios with acceptance narratives\n- **A.3 Business Rules**: Domain invariants in ubiquitous language\n- **A.4 Success Criteria**: Quantitative and qualitative\n- **A.5 Scope**: In/out with rationale\n- **A.6 Key Decisions**: Options considered, choice rationale, tradeoffs\n- **A.7 Risks & Mitigations**: Tabular\n- **A.8 Dependencies**: Upstream, downstream, external\n- **A.9 Glossary Check**: Terms used verified against glossary\n\n### What does NOT belong in Part A\n- Implementation details\n- Code structure\n- Database schema\n- API endpoints\n- Algorithm specifics\n\n(Those go in Part B.)\n\n## Part B Guidelines\n\n### Goal\nAgent can execute this section without re-reading Part A.\nStructured, unambiguous, machine-verifiable where possible.\n\n### What belongs in Part B\n\n- **B.1 Input Contract**: Exact shape (Python dataclass for domain, Pydantic for interfaces)\n- **B.2 Output Contract**: Exact shape with guarantees (multi-criteria, never single score)\n- **B.3 Core Logic Specification**: Algorithm or flow (pseudocode — NO LLM math, all numbers from code)\n- **B.4 Data Model Changes**: SQL migrations, schema changes\n- **B.5 Affected Bounded Contexts**: Which of 9 BCs impacted\n- **B.6 Domain Events Emitted**: With payload shape\n- **B.7 API Surface**: HTTP endpoints (Phase 2+ only) with request/response\n- **B.8 Non-Functional Requirements**: Performance, cost, reliability, observability\n- **B.9 Test Requirements**: Test pyramid allocation, BDD scenarios\n- **B.10 Implementation Constraints**: MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD\n- **B.11 Dependencies on Skills/Subagents**: Which to use\n- **B.12 Rollout Plan**: Feature flag, migration, rollback\n- **B.13 Verification Checklist**: Pre-merge checks\n\n### Relationship to Part A\n\nPart B **derives from** Part A but is not a summary.\n\n- Part A: \"Thesis output must present both bull and bear perspectives with citations\"\n- Part B (derived): \n  ```python\n  @dataclass\n  class ThesisSynthesis:\n      bull_case: BullAnalysis\n      bear_case: BearAnalysis  # MUST NOT be None or empty\n      catalysts: list[Catalyst]\n      risks: list[Risk]\n      # NO single confidence score — multi-criteria only\n      signal_tier_summary: SignalTierSummary  # Tier 1/2/3/4 agreement levels\n  \n  # Invariant: bear_case.is_substantive() must be True\n  ```\n\nIf you can't derive B from A, A is incomplete — revise A first.\n\n## Stock-Specific Part B Requirements\n\n### No LLM Math in B.3\n```\n## B.3 Core Logic\n\nStep 1: Fetch financial statements (code)\nStep 2: Compute PE ratio = price / eps (DETERMINISTIC PYTHON CODE)\nStep 3: LLM classifies PE level relative to sector range (LLM classification only)\nStep 4: Combine signal tiers (code — weighted aggregation)\n\nNOT: \"LLM computes PE ratio based on context\"  ← VIOLATION\n```\n\n### Multi-Criteria Output in B.2\n```python\n# CORRECT — multi-criteria\n@dataclass\nclass ThesisOutput:\n    ticker: Ticker\n    bull_case: BullAnalysis\n    bear_case: BearAnalysis\n    quant_signals: QuantSignals\n    sentiment_signals: SentimentSignals\n    recommendation_note: str  # framed as research aid, not buy/sell\n    as_of: datetime\n\n# WRONG — single score\n@dataclass\nclass ThesisOutput:\n    ticker: Ticker\n    buy_confidence: float  # ← VIOLATION: single score, no adversarial balance\n```\n\n## Deriving B from A — Process\n\nFor each section in Part A, ask:\n1. What does this imply for input/output?\n2. What data structures are needed?\n3. What events should fire?\n4. What can go wrong (edge cases)?\n5. How will this be tested?\n6. Does this require any number computation? → If yes, who computes it? (Must be code, not LLM)\n\nWork through Part A section by section. Write Part B section by section based on derivations.\n\n## Tiers\n\n### Tier 1 (Strategic)\n- 100-300 lines\n- One per major initiative (e.g., \"Four-Tier Signal Architecture\")\n- Rarely changes\n\n### Tier 2 (Feature)\n- 200-500 lines\n- One per feature capability (e.g., \"KOL Recommendation Extraction\")\n- Changes per iteration\n\n### Tier 3 (Task)\n- 50-150 lines\n- One per implementable task\n- Changes per session\n\nIf Tier 2 exceeds 500 lines → **split before shipping**.\n\n## Common Mistakes\n\n### Part A Too Technical\n```markdown\n## A.1 Context\nThe system uses Dramatiq queue to dispatch extraction jobs to Python workers \nwhich call Claude API with prompt caching enabled...\n```\n\n**Why wrong**: Implementation detail belongs in Part B.\n\n### Correct\n```markdown\n## A.1 Context\nKOL influencers on YouTube and Facebook measurably move VN stock prices.\nToday we have no systematic way to track which KOLs recommend which stocks\nand whether those recommendations turn out to be correct. This feature\ningests KOL content and extracts recommendations for calibration...\n```\n\n### Part B Too Narrative\n```markdown\n## B.1 Input Contract\nThe user provides a YouTube URL and the system extracts the recommendation.\nWe'll probably use Pydantic for validation...\n```\n\n**Why wrong**: Ambiguous, speculative.\n\n### Correct\n```python\n## B.1 Input Contract\n\n@dataclass\nclass ExtractKolRecommendationCommand:\n    kol_id: KolId\n    source_url: str  # YouTube video URL\n    published_at: datetime\n\n# Validation rules:\n# - source_url must be valid YouTube URL\n# - published_at must be in past\n```\n\n## Sample Workflow\n\n```\n1. Run /drill-me if new domain terms expected (e.g., \"KOL\", \"CredibilityScore\")\n2. Write Part A (narrative)\n3. Review Part A with user — does it capture intent?\n4. Write Part B (derive from A)\n5. Review Part B — every section maps to Part A? No LLM math in B.3?\n6. Fill Part C initial (authoring history)\n7. Save as specs/tierN/NNN-feature-name.md\n8. Run /spec-to-wiki for Obsidian view\n9. Schedule /bdd-planner for test plan\n10. Schedule /master-plan for implementation breakdown\n```\n\n## Quality Checklist (before finalizing)\n\n- [ ] Every domain term appears in glossary.md\n- [ ] Part A readable by non-engineer stakeholder\n- [ ] Part B sections derive from Part A\n- [ ] All MUST/MUST NOT constraints listed\n- [ ] Rollback plan specified\n- [ ] Test requirements concrete (not \"write tests\")\n- [ ] Risks identified with mitigation\n- [ ] Dependencies listed explicitly\n- [ ] B.3 logic has NO LLM math (numbers come from code)\n- [ ] B.2 output is multi-criteria (not single buy/sell score)\n- [ ] Bear case present if thesis-related\n\n## Related Skills\n\n- `ddd-tactical-patterns` — for domain-model aspects of specs\n- `evidence-extraction` — for specs touching evidence\n- `test-pyramid-balance` — for Part B.9 test requirements","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"7b0f681f-1aa0-4075-990f-db69059637d4","timestamp":"2026-04-29T14:51:20.412Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"---\nname: spec-dual-layer\ndescription: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). {"parentUuid":"7b0f681f-1aa0-4075-990f-db69059637d4","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":46,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"3c71b37b-3441-4455-8733-46743a195cc3","timestamp":"2026-04-29T14:51:20.428Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"c978bc8f-cbcf-4f05-8b71-88c7c187d000","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_019C79TY9raatbPAp888AgJx","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Hwsc7rsdbuyNeyY5h1SSWV","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\spec-dual-layer\\SKILL.md","content":"---\nname: spec-dual-layer\ndescription: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\nallowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Edit, Write]\n---\n\n# Skill: Dual-Layer Spec Authoring\n\n## Purpose\n\nEvery feature spec serves two audiences:\n- **Human stakeholder** needs narrative, context, rationale\n- **AI agent** needs structure, unambiguous contracts, machine-verifiable\n\nDual-layer specs serve both without compromise — Part A is for humans, Part B is for agents.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Writing any Tier 2 (feature) or Tier 3 (task) spec\n- Refactoring existing spec to dual-layer format\n- Reviewing a spec for completeness\n\n## Reference Template\n\n`/SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` at project root is canonical. Three parts:\n\n| Part | Audience | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Part A** — Business Specification | Stakeholder | Narrative — context, users, rules, success, decisions |\n| **Part B** — Agent Contract | Agent | Structured — input/output, logic, data model, tests, constraints |\n| **Part C** — Provenance & Review | Both | Living log — authoring history, review trail |\n\n## Part A vs Part B — Decision Rule\n\nIf the content is...\n\n| Content | Part |\n|---|---|\n| WHY this exists, WHAT problem it solves | A.1 Context |\n| WHO uses this, scenario narratives | A.2 Users + Use Cases |\n| Domain invariants in ubiquitous language | A.3 Business Rules |\n| Quantitative success criteria | A.4 Success Criteria |\n| In/out scope with rationale | A.5 Scope |\n| Options + chosen path + tradeoffs | A.6 Key Decisions |\n| Risk table | A.7 Risks |\n| Glossary check | A.9 |\n| Exact dataclass / DTO shape | B.1 Input / B.2 Output |\n| Algorithm / pseudocode | B.3 Core Logic |\n| SQL migrations | B.4 Data Model Changes |\n| BC impact list | B.5 Affected BCs |\n| Domain events with payload | B.6 |\n| HTTP routes (Phase 2+) | B.7 API Surface |\n| Performance / cost / SLO | B.8 NFR |\n| Test pyramid allocation | B.9 Test Requirements |\n| MUST / MUST NOT lists | B.10 Implementation Constraints |\n| Skill / subagent dependencies | B.11 |\n| Feature flag + rollback plan | B.12 Rollout |\n| Pre-merge checklist | B.13 Verification |\n\nIf you can't derive Part B from Part A → Part A is incomplete; revise A first.\n\nSee `references/section-checklists.md` for full section-by-section content lists.\n\n## Stock-Specific Part B Rules\n\n### B.3 — No LLM Math\n\nLogic that produces a number MUST be deterministic code. The LLM only classifies pre-computed values.\n\n```\n# CORRECT\nStep 1: Fetch financial statements (code)\nStep 2: pe = compute_pe(price, eps)               # DETERMINISTIC\nStep 3: LLM classifies pe vs sector range          # CLASSIFICATION ONLY\nStep 4: Combine signal tiers (code aggregation)\n\n# WRONG — VIOLATION (I-S1)\nStep 2: \"LLM computes PE ratio based on context\"\n```\n\n### B.2 — Multi-Criteria Output, Never Single Score\n\n```python\n# CORRECT — multi-criteria\n@dataclass\nclass ThesisOutput:\n    ticker: Ticker\n    bull_case: BullAnalysis\n    bear_case: BearAnalysis              # MUST be substantive\n    quant_signals: QuantSignals\n    sentiment_signals: SentimentSignals\n    recommendation_note: str             # framed as research aid\n    as_of: datetime\n\n# WRONG — single score (charter principle 2 violation)\n@dataclass\nclass ThesisOutput:\n    buy_confidence: float                # ← VIOLATION\n```\n\n## Tier Sizing\n\n| Tier | Lines | Cadence |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Tier 1** Strategic | 100–300 | Rarely changes (e.g., \"Four-Tier Signal Architecture\") |\n| **Tier 2** Feature | 200–500 | Per iteration. Split before shipping if > 500 |\n| **Tier 3** Task | 50–150 | Per session |\n\n## Deriving Part B from Part A — Process\n\nFor each section in Part A, ask:\n1. What does this imply for input/output shape?\n2. What data structures are needed?\n3. What domain events should fire?\n4. What can go wrong (edge cases)?\n5. How will this be tested (pyramid layer)?\n6. Does any number computation appear? → If yes, who computes it? **Must be code, never LLM.**\n\nWork A → B section-by-section. Don't skip step 6.\n\n## Validation Pre-Conditions (Quality Checklist)\n\n- [ ] Every domain term appears in `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md`\n- [ ] Part A readable by non-engineer stakeholder (no implementation detail)\n- [ ] Every Part B section derives from Part A content\n- [ ] All MUST / MUST NOT constraints listed in B.10\n- [ ] Rollback plan in B.12\n- [ ] Test requirements concrete (not \"write tests\")\n- [ ] Risks identified with mitigation in A.7\n- [ ] Dependencies listed explicitly (A.8 + B.11)\n- [ ] B.3 logic has NO LLM math (numbers come from code)\n- [ ] B.2 output is multi-criteria (not single buy/sell score)\n- [ ] Bear case present and substantive if thesis-related\n\n## Sample Workflow\n\n1. Run `/drill-me` if new domain terms expected (e.g., \"KOL\", \"CredibilityScore\")\n2. Write Part A\n3. Review Part A with user — does it capture intent?\n4. Write Part B (derive from A; no LLM math; multi-criteria)\n5. Review Part B section-by-section\n6. Fill Part C initial authoring history\n7. Save as `specs/tierN/NNN-feature-name.md`\n8. Run `/spec-to-wiki` for Obsidian view\n9. Schedule `/bdd-planner` for test plan\n10. Schedule `/master-plan` for implementation breakdown\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- **Part A too technical** (\"system uses Dramatiq queue...\") → implementation detail goes in B.3 / B.5\n- **Part B too narrative** (\"we'll probably use Pydantic for validation\") → write the actual `@dataclass` shape\n- **Mixing audiences in one section** — split into Part A explanation + Part B contract\n- **Skipping Part C** — provenance log dies first; add at authoring, append at every review\n\nSee `references/section-checklists.md` for full wrong-vs-correct examples.\n\n## See Also\n\n- `references/section-checklists.md` — full Part A.1–A.9 + Part B.1–B.13 content lists + wrong/correct examples\n- `/SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` — canonical template\n- `ddd-tactical-patterns` SKILL.md — domain-model aspects\n- `evidence-extraction` SKILL.md — for specs touching evidence\n- `test-pyramid-balance` SKILL.md — for B.9 test requirements\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":7816,"cache_read_input_tokens":248159,"output_tokens":5131,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":7816,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":5131,"cache_read_input_tokens":248159,"cache_creation_input_tokens":7816,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":7816},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYFXdzaoFyhViiUmZbuD","type":"assistant","uuid":"c5f9ccb8-f39e-444b-bf48-0c3ad1f46a7e","timestamp":"2026-04-29T14:52:07.763Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

How will this be tested (pyramid layer)?\n6. Does any number computation appear? → If yes, who computes it? **Must be code, never LLM.**\n\nWork A → B section-by-section. Don't skip step 6.\n\n## Validation Pre-Conditions (Quality Checklist)\n\n- [ ] Every domain term appears in `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md`\n- [ ] Part A readable by non-engineer stakeholder (no implementation detail)\n- [ ] Every Part B section derives from Part A content\n- [ ] All MUST / MUST NOT constraints listed in B.10\n- [ ] Rollback plan in B.12\n- [ ] Test requirements concrete (not \"write tests\")\n- [ ] Risks identified with mitigation in A.7\n- [ ] Dependencies listed explicitly (A.8 + B.11)\n- [ ] B.3 logic has NO LLM math (numbers come from code)\n- [ ] B.2 output is multi-criteria (not single buy/sell score)\n- [ ] Bear case present and substantive if thesis-related\n\n## Sample Workflow\n\n1. Run `/drill-me` if new domain terms expected (e.g., \"KOL\", \"CredibilityScore\")\n2. Write Part A\n3. Review Part A with user — does it capture intent?\n4. Write Part B (derive from A; no LLM math; multi-criteria)\n5. Review Part B section-by-section\n6. Fill Part C initial authoring history\n7. Save as `specs/tierN/NNN-feature-name.md`\n8. Run `/spec-to-wiki` for Obsidian view\n9. Schedule `/bdd-planner` for test plan\n10. Schedule `/master-plan` for implementation breakdown\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- **Part A too technical** (\"system uses Dramatiq queue...\") → implementation detail goes in B.3 / B.5\n- **Part B too narrative** (\"we'll probably use Pydantic for validation\") → write the actual `@dataclass` shape\n- **Mixing audiences in one section** — split into Part A explanation + Part B contract\n- **Skipping Part C** — provenance log dies first; add at authoring, append at every review\n\nSee `references/section-checklists.md` for full wrong-vs-correct examples.\n\n## See Also\n\n- `references/section-checklists.md` — full Part A.1–A.9 + Part B.1–B.13 content lists + wrong/correct examples\n- `/SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` — canonical template\n- `ddd-tactical-patterns` SKILL.md — domain-model aspects\n- `evidence-extraction` SKILL.md — for specs touching evidence\n- `test-pyramid-balance` SKILL.md — for B.9 test requirements\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":243,"newStart":1,"newLines":163,"lines":[" ---"," name: spec-dual-layer"," description: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n---\n\n# Skill: Dual-Layer Spec Authoring\n\n## Purpose\n\nEvery feature spec serves two audiences with different needs:\n- **Human stakeholder**: narrative, context, rationale\n- **AI agent**: structure, unambiguous contracts, machine-verifiable\n\nThis skill teaches the dual-layer pattern for specs that serve both.\n\n## When to Use\n\n- Writing any Tier 2 (feature) spec\n- Writing any Tier 3 (task) spec\n- Refactoring existing spec to dual-layer format\n- Reviewing a spec for completeness\n\n## The Template\n\nReference: `/SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` at project root.\n\nThree parts:\n- **Part A**: Business Specification (narrative)\n- **Part B**: Agent Contract (structured)\n- **Part C**: Provenance & Review (living log)\n\n## Part A Guidelines\n\n### Goal\nMake it readable by non-engineer stakeholders. Business Analyst mindset.\n\n### What belongs in Part A\n\n- **A.1 Context**: Why this exists, what problem it solves, narrative\n- **A.2 User & Use Cases**: Who uses this, concrete scenarios with acceptance narratives\n- **A.3 Business Rules**: Domain invariants in ubiquitous language\n- **A.4 Success Criteria**: Quantitative and qualitative\n- **A.5 Scope**: In/out with rationale\n- **A.6 Key Decisions**: Options considered, choice rationale, tradeoffs\n- **A.7 Risks & Mitigations**: Tabular\n- **A.8 Dependencies**: Upstream, downstream, external\n- **A.9 Glossary Check**: Terms used verified against glossary\n\n### What does NOT belong in Part A\n- Implementation details\n- Code structure\n- Database schema\n- API endpoints\n- Algorithm specifics\n\n(Those go in Part B.)\n\n## Part B Guidelines\n\n### Goal\nAgent can execute this section without re-reading Part A.\nStructured, unambiguous, machine-verifiable where possible.\n\n### What belongs in Part B\n\n- **B.1 Input Contract**: Exact shape (Python dataclass for domain, Pydantic for interfaces)\n- **B.2 Output Contract**: Exact shape with guarantees (multi-criteria, never single score)\n- **B.3 Core Logic Specification**: Algorithm or flow (pseudocode — NO LLM math, all numbers from code)\n- **B.4 Data Model Changes**: SQL migrations, schema changes\n- **B.5 Affected Bounded Contexts**: Which of 9 BCs impacted\n- **B.6 Domain Events Emitted**: With payload shape\n- **B.7 API Surface**: HTTP endpoints (Phase 2+ only) with request/response\n- **B.8 Non-Functional Requirements**: Performance, cost, reliability, observability\n- **B.9 Test Requirements**: Test pyramid allocation, BDD scenarios\n- **B.10 Implementation Constraints**: MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD\n- **B.11 Dependencies on Skills/Subagents**: Which to use\n- **B.12 Rollout Plan**: Feature flag, migration, rollback\n- **B.13 Verification Checklist**: Pre-merge checks\n\n### Relationship to Part A\n\nPart B **derives from** Part A but is not a summary.\n\n- Part A: \"Thesis output must present both bull and bear perspectives with citations\"\n- Part B (derived): \n  ```python\n  @dataclass\n  class ThesisSynthesis:\n      bull_case: BullAnalysis\n      bear_case: BearAnalysis  # MUST NOT be None or empty\n      catalysts: list[Catalyst]\n      risks: list[Risk]\n      # NO single confidence score — multi-criteria only\n      signal_tier_summary: SignalTierSummary  # Tier 1/2/3/4 agreement levels\n  \n  # Invariant: bear_case.is_substantive() must be True\n  ```\n\nIf you can't derive B from A, A is incomplete — revise A first.\n\n## Stock-Specific Part B Requirements\n\n### No LLM Math in B.3\n```\n## B.3 Core Logic\n\nStep 1: Fetch financial statements (code)\nStep 2: Compute PE ratio = price / eps (DETERMINISTIC PYTHON CODE)\nStep 3: LLM classifies PE level relative to sector range (LLM classification only)\nStep 4: Combine signal tiers (code — weighted aggregation)\n\nNOT: \"LLM computes PE ratio based on context\"  ← VIOLATION\n```\n\n### Multi-Criteria Output in B.2\n```python\n# CORRECT — multi-criteria\n@dataclass\nclass ThesisOutput:\n    ticker: Ticker\n    bull_case: BullAnalysis\n    bear_case: BearAnalysis\n    quant_signals: QuantSignals\n    sentiment_signals: SentimentSignals\n    recommendation_note: str  # framed as research aid, not buy/sell\n    as_of: datetime\n\n# WRONG — single score\n@dataclass\nclass ThesisOutput:\n    ticker: Ticker\n    buy_confidence: float  # ← VIOLATION: single score, no adversarial balance\n```\n\n## Deriving B from A — Process\n\nFor each section in Part A, ask:\n1. What does this imply for input/output?\n2. What data structures are needed?\n3. What events should fire?\n4. What can go wrong (edge cases)?\n5. How will this be tested?\n6. Does this require any number computation? → If yes, who computes it? (Must be code, not LLM)\n\nWork through Part A section by section. Write Part B section by section based on derivations.\n\n## Tiers\n\n### Tier 1 (Strategic)\n- 100-300 lines\n- One per major initiative (e.g., \"Four-Tier Signal Architecture\")\n- Rarely changes\n\n### Tier 2 (Feature)\n- 200-500 lines\n- One per feature capability (e.g., \"KOL Recommendation Extraction\")\n- Changes per iteration\n\n### Tier 3 (Task)\n- 50-150 lines\n- One per implementable task\n- Changes per session\n\nIf Tier 2 exceeds 500 lines → **split before shipping**.\n\n## Common Mistakes\n\n### Part A Too Technical\n```markdown\n## A.1 Context\nThe system uses Dramatiq queue to dispatch extraction jobs to Python workers \nwhich call Claude API with prompt caching enabled...\n```\n\n**Why wrong**: Implementation detail belongs in Part B.\n\n### Correct\n```markdown\n## A.1 Context\nKOL influencers on YouTube and Facebook measurably move VN stock prices.\nToday we have no systematic way to track which KOLs recommend which stocks\nand whether those recommendations turn out to be correct. This feature\ningests KOL content and extracts recommendations for calibration...\n```\n\n### Part B Too Narrative\n```markdown\n## B.1 Input Contract\nThe user provides a YouTube URL and the system extracts the recommendation.\nWe'll probably use Pydantic for validation...\n```\n\n**Why wrong**: Ambiguous, speculative.\n\n### Correct\n```python\n## B.1 Input Contract\n\n@dataclass\nclass ExtractKolRecommendationCommand:\n    kol_id: KolId\n    source_url: str  # YouTube video URL\n    published_at: datetime\n\n# Validation rules:\n# - source_url must be valid YouTube URL\n# - published_at must be in past\n```\n\n## Sample Workflow\n\n```\n1. Run /drill-me if new domain terms expected (e.g., \"KOL\", \"CredibilityScore\")\n2. Write Part A (narrative)\n3. Review Part A with user — does it capture intent?\n4. Write Part B (derive from A)\n5. Review Part B — every section maps to Part A? No LLM math in B.3?\n6. Fill Part C initial (authoring history)\n7. Save as specs/tierN/NNN-feature-name.md\n8. Run /spec-to-wiki for Obsidian view\n9. Schedule /bdd-planner for test plan\n10. Schedule /master-plan for implementation breakdown\n```\n\n## Quality Checklist (before finalizing)\n\n- [ ] Every domain term appears in glossary.md\n- [ ] Part A readable by non-engineer stakeholder\n- [ ] Part B sections derive from Part A\n- [ ] All MUST/MUST NOT constraints listed\n- [ ] Rollback plan specified\n- [ ] Test requirements concrete (not \"write tests\")\n- [ ] Risks identified with mitigation\n- [ ] Dependencies listed explicitly\n- [ ] B.3 logic has NO LLM math (numbers come from code)\n- [ ] B.2 output is multi-criteria (not single buy/sell score)\n- [ ] Bear case present if thesis-related\n\n## Related Skills\n\n- `ddd-tactical-patterns` — for domain-model aspects of specs\n- `evidence-extraction` — for specs touching evidence\n- `test-pyramid-balance` — for Part B.9 test requirements\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"c5f9ccb8-f39e-444b-bf48-0c3ad1f46a7e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"1cbc4259-d85c-4007-b5f7-acbe9c6447e4","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_019C79TY9raatbPAp888AgJx","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01AkQ9QuQKHtxp4RzSGAnpry","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\.claude\\skills\\spec-dual-layer\\references\\section-checklists.md","content":"# Spec Section Checklists — Part A & Part B\n\n> Reference companion to `../SKILL.md`. Full content lists per section.\n\n## Part A — Business Specification\n\n### A.1 Context\n- Why this exists\n- What problem it solves\n- Narrative framing for non-engineer reader\n\n### A.2 User & Use Cases\n- Who uses this (persona / role)\n- Concrete scenarios\n- Acceptance narratives (\"when X happens, user expects Y\")\n\n### A.3 Business Rules\n- Domain invariants in ubiquitous-language terms\n- Reference glossary entries\n\n### A.4 Success Criteria\n- Quantitative measures (e.g., \"extraction precision ≥ 80% on eval set N=200\")\n- Qualitative measures (e.g., \"thesis output frames as research aid, not advice\")\n\n### A.5 Scope\n- In: explicit feature list\n- Out: explicit non-features with rationale (prevents scope creep)\n\n### A.6 Key Decisions\n- Options considered\n- Choice rationale\n- Tradeoffs accepted\n\n### A.7 Risks & Mitigations\nTabular:\n\n| Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |\n|---|---|---|---|\n\n### A.8 Dependencies\n- Upstream (what feeds this)\n- Downstream (what consumes this)\n- External (third-party services / data sources)\n\n### A.9 Glossary Check\n- Every domain term used in this spec → verified in `agent-workspace/ubiquitous-language/glossary.md`\n\n### What does NOT belong in Part A\n\n- Implementation details\n- Code structure\n- Database schema\n- API endpoints\n- Algorithm specifics\n\n(Those go in Part B.)\n\n---\n\n## Part B — Agent Contract\n\nGoal: agent can execute this section without re-reading Part A.\n\n### B.1 Input Contract\nExact shape — Python dataclass for domain, Pydantic for interfaces:\n\n```python\n@dataclass\nclass ExtractKolRecommendationCommand:\n    kol_id: KolId\n    source_url: str  # YouTube video URL\n    published_at: datetime\n\n# Validation rules:\n# - source_url must be valid YouTube URL\n# - published_at must be in past\n```\n\n### B.2 Output Contract\nExact shape with guarantees. Multi-criteria, never single score.\n\n### B.3 Core Logic Specification\nAlgorithm or flow as pseudocode. NO LLM math — all numbers from deterministic code; LLM only classifies.\n\n### B.4 Data Model Changes\nSQL migrations, schema changes (see `postgres-pgvector` skill for shape).\n\n### B.5 Affected Bounded Contexts\nList which of the 9 BCs are impacted (see `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md`).\n\n### B.6 Domain Events Emitted\nEach event with payload shape.\n\n### B.7 API Surface\nHTTP endpoints (Phase 2+ only). Each item enforceable by hook or human review.\n\n---\n\n## Relationship: B Derives From A\n\nExample:\n- **Part A**: \"Thesis output must present both bull and bear perspectives with citations\"\n- **Part B (derived)**:\n\n```python\n@dataclass\nclass ThesisSynthesis:\n    bull_case: BullAnalysis\n    bear_case: BearAnalysis    # MUST NOT be None or empty\n    catalysts: list[Catalyst]\n    risks: list[Risk]\n    signal_tier_summary: SignalTierSummary  # Tier 1/2/3/4 agreement levels\n\n# Invariant: bear_case.is_substantive() must be True\n```\n\nIf you can't derive B from A → A is incomplete.\n\n---\n\n## Common Mistakes — Wrong vs Correct\n\n### Part A too technical\n\n**Wrong**:\n```markdown\n## A.1 Context\nThe system uses Dramatiq queue to dispatch extraction jobs to Python workers\nwhich call Claude API with prompt caching enabled...\n```\n\n**Correct**:\n```markdown\n## A.1 Context\nKOL influencers on YouTube and Facebook measurably move VN stock prices.\nToday we have no systematic way to track which KOLs recommend which stocks\nand whether those recommendations turn out to be correct. This feature\ningests KOL content and extracts recommendations for calibration...\n```\n\n### Part B too narrative\n\n**Wrong**:\n```markdown\n## B.1 Input Contract\nThe user provides a YouTube URL and the system extracts the recommendation.\nWe'll probably use Pydantic for validation...\n```\n\n**Correct**:\n```python\n## B.1 Input Contract\n\n@dataclass\nclass ExtractKolRecommendationCommand:\n    kol_id: KolId\n    source_url: str  # YouTube video URL\n    published_at: datetime\n\n# Validation rules:\n# - source_url must be valid YouTube URL\n# - published_at must be in past\n```\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":7816,"cache_read_input_tokens":248159,"output_tokens":5131,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":7816,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":5131,"cache_read_input_tokens":248159,"cache_creation_input_tokens":7816,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":7816},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaYFXdzaoFyhViiUmZbuD","type":"assistant","uuid":"22d9cbbd-786b-4f23-999e-2f37f9eb5a8b","timestamp":"2026-04-29T14:52:33.588Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"1691a5a8-8de7-439a-834f-1e05173f2431","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

Multi-criteria, never single score.\n\n### B.3 Core Logic Specification\nAlgorithm or flow as pseudocode. {"parentUuid":"f26bbf1a-ed5d-4188-b7f0-6425f1343c33","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability.
